  **Established.** In Qwen3-8B a rank-1 or rank-2 subspace of the task specification states at blocks 12 to 23 is a steering handle on the algorithm that matches or exceeds the full-state exchange for ban sources and for the forced Floyd-Warshall, quickselect, counting sort and DFS sources; recovers 0.17 to 0.43 of forced Bellman-Ford/SPFA and 0.06 to 0.53 of forced BFS; rank 2 untested for forced sources. It routes more cleanly than the full state on one task (shortest path: Floyd-Warshall 28/28 against 8/20); on kth smallest the DAS edit changes the implementation form (mostly an array of counts against the full state's dictionary with sorted keys), not the algorithm. The handle is not a certified variable, because permuted labels and an untrained network admit it (the untrained-network control ran on shortest path only; the committed comparison with the diverged contrastive fit (ratio 0.013) proved meaningless and was replaced post hoc; under the matched likelihood fit the untrained network gains 43.6 nats against 8.6 for the trained one (ratio 5.1), while the fit-value ratio is 0.92 (13.31 against 14.45 nats)) (iteration-8 correction). In Gemma the analogous subspace at the fork passes the random-subspace, permuted-label and untrained-network controls (dormancy checks not run; its natural variance lies below the random 95th percentile at ranks 1, 2 and 4, and it recovers 1.98 to 2.81 times the full-state swap) and, with the shared opening prefilled, acts as a dose dial that keeps the programs; the Qwen3-8B and Gemma controls used different objectives, readouts and permutation schemes, so their outcomes are not directly comparable (iteration-8 correction). Where a fork of a single token exists, temperature acts on the algorithm through the fork logits divided by T, as predicted before sampling on one Qwen3-8B unit and on Gemma; on the collapsed tasks the fork margins put the alternative out of temperature's reach. On connected components the decision falls at the token that names the routine, and the effect of a random push is already expressed at that token: a teacher-forced readout of the fork margin matches the sampled outcomes at Spearman 0.80 (the 48-token opening log-likelihood ratio at 0.87), through the probability that stays on the default fork tokens rather than through which algorithm each other token leads to (a placebo that shuffles the token map reaches 0.80 in 18% of permutations); no direction-level property predicted which pushes move the fork (axis 0.17 and 0.01; plan-subspace projection 0.03 in iteration 4) (iteration-8 correction). The weak plan noise of iteration 5 came from its dose unit; profile and energy each carry part of the effect on connected components (profile +0.22 [0.08, 0.36], energy +0.18 [0.06, 0.30]); the shortest-path profile contrast is confounded by a massive-activation cell holding 82% of the unit's energy (iteration-8 correction). Evolutionary search with an evaluator reaches known techniques outside the catalogue on kth smallest: search 78 of 2,500 calls (0.0312 [0.0247, 0.0388], 12 merged clusters) against 2 of 500 calls (0.0040 [0.0005, 0.0144], 1 merged cluster) for the instruction alone (rate ratio 7.8, lower 95% bound 2.41, short of the committed 10x), 0 of 1,250 for enumerate and pick and 0 of 500 without evolution; the larger mutator reached 23 of 500 calls (0.0460 [0.0294, 0.0682], 7 merged clusters); about five techniques in all (value-range binary search, Fenwick tree order statistics, a treap, bucket select, partial selection sort) (iteration-8 correction).

  **Ruled out.** The axis from the default to the second choice as the channel of random pushes (disconfirmed and not mediating). Discreteness of the effect of the fitted edit. The seeds as the cause of the null of iteration 5. Temperature above 1 as a source of a new idea: on every unit it only reweighted the algorithms the fork already weighs. Search at ten times the best text knob's level a rate on two tasks.

  **Dead ends.** The committed contrastive DAS objective, which diverged and broke programs, was replaced by the likelihood objective. The transcoder attribution graph in Gemma was dropped after three attempts on a 16 GB GPU. The judge gate for novelty failed for every judge family in the search experiment, so its classes rest on manual and rule-based reads. A top five push inside the forced prompt manifold of the grid task produced no algorithm outside the five in 300 programs, which closes the push route for that question at the doses tried.

  **Not run.** Plan resampling and the DAS-coordinate top-five placement on the grid task (the T1 extension) were dropped by the DAS experiment's committed drop order (deviation D-drop, Section 7.3.10); the untrained-network control ran on shortest path only (iteration-8 correction).

  ## 7.11 What the next iteration takes from this one

  The next iteration takes four leads. First, the DAS handle in Qwen3-8B needs the control it failed: a fit whose versions with permuted labels and with an untrained network do not transfer, which may require fitting at the fork in generation, where Gemma's controls passed, rather than at the task specification states; because the Qwen3-8B and Gemma controls used different objectives, readouts and permutation schemes, their outcomes are not directly comparable, and a matched protocol is part of that test (iteration-8 correction). Second, shortest path decides late, so the fork claim needs a measure that follows the decision to where it happens (the opening LLR improved from 48 to 160 tokens). Third, the temperature claim held on two of four mixed units; the misses on trapped rain water, which has a second opening with its own split, and valid anagram, where a second decision (fixed array against hash map) follows a few tokens after the fork, call for a prediction that composes more than one fork. Fourth, evolutionary search found known techniques outside the catalogue on kth smallest at 0.031 per call against 0.004 for the instruction alone (ratio 7.8, lower bound 2.41, short of the committed 10x; iteration-8 correction), so a search on a task whose catalogue already covers the known techniques, where a correct program outside it would be new, is the remaining route to a novel algorithm. Two items not run in iteration 7 carry forward: plan resampling and the DAS-coordinate top-five placement on the grid task (Section 7.3.10) (iteration-8 correction).

  # Iteration 8: temperature at the fork, one DAS protocol for two families, a circuit in Qwen3-8B, a fair test of Gemma's dial, a temperature law on held-out families, and a top-five prohibition across ten configurations

  ## 8.1 Why this iteration ran what it ran

  **The review of the iteration-7 record.** The review was blocking. It raised eleven items, six of them marked as needing a fix before any new claim. The first said the kth smallest results rested on a labeller gap: the frozen runtime rule sent "count the values, then sort the distinct keys" to the class other, so 35 programs that implement counting sort in dictionary form were read as programs outside the catalogue, and the pooled DAS recovery on that task was inflated. The second asked for the DAS recovery of iteration 7 by source and rank, because a pooled number hid that forced BFS and forced Bellman-Ford/SPFA sources recovered far less than the ban sources, and it asked what the three untrained-network ratios in the record measured. The third found that the Gemma dial had been compared with a forced-BFS prompt sampled without the 32-token shared opening that every dial cell had prefilled, so "42 against 35" compared two conditionings. The fourth asked that the fork margin be stated as a readout of a push's effect rather than as a predictor of it. The fifth asked for the natural-variance numbers and dormancy checks of the Gemma subspace, which the record had passed by a flag that fired on a correlation threshold alone. The sixth asked that the positioning of iteration 7 be verified live, venue by venue. The five minor items asked for a list of what iteration 7 did not run, fresh-slot rows for the dose unit table, search results stated as rates per call with merged clusters, a per-unit statement of the temperature claim's scope, and the repair of four stale tags and ten lost file names.

  **The hypothesis update.** Iteration 7 left one finding that every later test could build on: on the tasks where it can be located, the algorithm is fixed by one or two generated tokens after a shared opening, the fork of Section 7.1. The update narrowed the plan-and-fork account to that token. We call the narrowed account the *one-token account*: whatever changes the algorithm a model writes (temperature, a prompt, an internal edit) changes the odds at the fork, the odds can be read before sampling from teacher-forced logits, and the components that compute them can be found and steered. The artifacts of this iteration call the fork the *decision token*; this section keeps the word fork. Seven claims were preregistered, each with a rule committed by sha256 before its first decisive sample. We call them by their content.

  - *The fork-dosing claim* (primary): temperature applied only at the fork, at a dose read off the fork's teacher-forced logits and a map from fork tokens to algorithms, gives the alternatives in the shares predicted before sampling and at no correctness cost; on connected components, where the twin writes union-find in every sample, it reaches a correct-only Hill-1 of at least 1.8 at a pass cost of at most 5 points while every global knob stays at or below 1.15. The claim also predicted that the fork's entropy does not stand out among the program's tokens, so that samplers triggered by entropy would miss it.
  - *The reachability claim*: forcing each of the fork's 64 most probable tokens reaches at least one correct known idea that no sampling knob reaches, on at least three units, and none of them is novel.
  - *The matched DAS claim*: under one protocol for both families, the fork holds a certified low-rank variable for the algorithm in Qwen3-8B and in Gemma, and the task band of Qwen3-8B (blocks 12 to 23 at the task specification positions) works in generation but fails the reverse, retention and clamp tests.
  - *The circuit claim*: in Qwen3-8B, a path-patching circuit computes the fork margin on two contrasts, its nodes beat matched random components in the real model, steering its top five nodes changes the written algorithm more than a matched random five, and its shape matches the circuit of Gemma's fork (Section 7.8).
  - *The Gemma dial claim*: at Gemma's grid fork, a forced-BFS prompt with the shared opening prefilled reaches at least 40 of 50 correct BFS programs, so that the dial and prompting tie under matched conditioning; the dial also works in free generation; and the subspace passes the dormancy checks that Qwen3-8B's handle failed.
  - *The temperature-law claim*: a law composed over one or two forks found by a blind locator predicts the temperature response of the algorithm mix within a mean total variation distance of 0.10 on at least 70% of units, including at least 3 of at least 4 held-out units in two families on which the law was never developed.
  - *The top-five prohibition claim*: among ten open configurations, at least one obeys a ban of its own five most used path algorithms with correct programs in at least 20% of samples, and on that model's manifold of ten forced algorithms the survivors land at the edge of the banned five rather than on the opposite side.

  **The strategy.** Seven artifacts ran (Table 374). The record audit repaired the iteration-7 record from rows on disk. A fork-dosing experiment tested temperature at the fork against every common knob and ran the forced branches of the reachability claim. A DAS experiment ran one protocol with seven committed controls at the fork of both families and at Qwen3-8B's task band. A circuit experiment ported the Gemma circuit pipeline of iteration 7 to Qwen3-8B. A Gemma experiment ran the prefill-matched prompting cells, a free-generation dial and the dormancy checks. A temperature-law experiment tested the composed law on three families, with Gemma and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct [22] held out, and compared Qwen3-8B with its base model at the fork. A prohibition experiment screened ten configurations under a ban of five names and placed the survivors on the selected model's manifold.

  ## 8.2 The record audit: 84 corrections, counting sort in dictionary form, and the checks the review named

  The record audit  read the iteration-7 report against the rows on disk and wrote 84 corrections, each marked as an iteration-8 correction. The report this section is appended to was byte-identical to the audit's input, so all 84 corrections applied exactly once, in place, and the result equals the audit's corrected report. Of the 141 values the corrections touch, 68 match the rows, 63 are new, 7 are corrected and 3 are carried from an earlier artifact (Table 375).

  **Counting sort in dictionary form.** The audit added one recogniser to the kth smallest labeller, mapped to the existing class counting sort, and validated it before relabelling any row. One revision was needed: the first version required a plain dictionary in the runtime tracer's record of dictionary sizes, which the tracer does not keep for `collections.Counter`. Table 376 gives the validation and the relabel. The relabel changed 35 of the 960 kth smallest rows, all from other to counting sort, and the old rules reproduce every stored label. With it, the full-state exchange of the forced counting sort source gives 29 of 30 counting sort programs (the 30th is a binary search on the value range that the rule calls quickselect), and the pooled kth smallest recovery of the DAS map falls from 1.59, 1.57 and 1.55 to 1.01 [0.95, 1.08], 1.00 [0.93, 1.08] and 0.99 [0.92, 1.06] at ranks 1, 4 and 16. The recovery of random subspaces (0.05) and the transfers of the fits with permuted labels do not change; those transfers are absolute shares of the 30 slots (0.47 to 0.70), and relative to the full-state effect they are 1.40, 1.24 and 0.82. The 36 catalogue variants that Section 7.3.9 listed among the correct programs outside the catalogue are mostly this one cell: 29 of them come from it and 6 more from the forced counting sort prompts.

On kth smallest the DAS edit changes the implementation form, not the algorithm: at rank 16, 28 of 30 DAS programs are an array of counts, while the full state's programs are a dictionary with sorted keys.   ## 8.3 Temperature at the fork (Qwen3-8B and Gemma)

  The fork-dosing experiment  asked whether temperature, applied only where the model commits to an algorithm, is the creativity knob that global temperature failed to be. We call the knob *fork-dosed temperature*: temperature d over the 20 most probable candidates at the fork, temperature 1 at every other position, with the dose read off the fork's teacher-forced logits and a token map (the algorithm each fork token leads to, from forced continuations) and committed before any sample. Two doses were committed per unit, which we call the low dose and the high dose; the low dose targets a minority share set in advance. Each cell has 50 slots of common random numbers (five prompt templates by ten random streams, the same in every arm), so changes of the fork token and of the algorithm are paired per slot. The comparators were global temperature 1.3, 1.6 and 2.0 with top-p 0.95, and min-p sampling [138] at threshold 0.1 and T 3.0. Two adaptive samplers were added: entropy-triggered temperature in the style of EDT [137] (T 2 wherever the token's entropy exceeds the twin's 90th percentile) and block-start temperature in the style of AdapT [32] (T 2 at the start of each code block). Two placebos put the high dose at the highest-entropy position or at a random position, and class-uniform forcing draws the fork token's algorithm class uniformly. Five commits were hash-chained: the protocol, the dose table with every per-arm prediction, the locator verdict, the reachability predictions, and one amendment.

The dial reaches DFS where global temperature cannot: 18% at the high dose against at most 4% for every global knob, and 7 correct off-default flips against 1 for global T 2.0. It pays for them, because seven of the fork's 20 candidates are tokens that break the program ('_parent', '-parent' and '父' fail 10 of 10 continuations). Forcing the fork class uniformly writes BFS 24 times, but only one of those BFS programs passes: the model's own BFS for this task is buggy.

  **The amendment.** After the primary cells were seen, one amendment was committed before its samples. It applies the same dose rules to the 20 candidates without the tokens whose committed continuations fail at least half the time (8 tokens at index 10 and 4 at index 11 on connected components; 13 tokens in Gemma, including ' queue'). No removed token was ever drawn (0 of 100 slots on connected components). The filter removes the breakage (pass cost 0.02) but not the ceiling: DFS rises to 0.18 at the low dose and 0.12 at the high dose, against predictions of 0.12 and 0.17 (mean absolute error 0.023 and 0.024), and correct-only Hill-1 reaches 1.54, which beats the best comparator family by +0.38 (lower bound +0.01, p 0.022) but stays short of 1.8. The alternative does not hold more than about 19% of the mass among the fork's 20 candidates, so no dose at that token reaches the target.

  [FIGURE:fig_forkdose_hill]

  **Where the fork sits in the entropy profile.** The claim predicted that the fork would not stand out by entropy, so that entropy-triggered samplers would miss it. The opposite holds. Code tokens are nearly deterministic, so the 90th percentile of the twin's per-token entropies is only 0.0003 to 0.05 nats, and the fork's entropy at T 1 lies above it in all 209 twin samples that reach the fork on the five located units (median 0.13 nats on connected components and 0.53 to 0.81 nats on the mixed units). The fork is also the single highest-entropy position among the first 64 tokens on 44 of 44 (Gemma), 32 of 39 (minimum spanning tree) and 21 of 39 (valid anagram) slots, but on 2 of 50 (connected components) and 0 of 37 (trapped rain water), the two units where a highest-entropy rule misses it. A rule that doses the highest-entropy position therefore finds the fork on most slots of three of the four mixed units (on every Gemma slot, where it reproduces the fork-dosed arm exactly, but on only 21 of 39 valid anagram slots) and misses it on trapped rain water and on the collapsed connected components (iteration-9 correction). This places the fork among the high-entropy minority tokens that Wang et al. find drive reinforcement learning on reasoning traces [139]. The threshold rule of the entropy-triggered sampler fires on about 10% of all tokens and spends most of its temperature away from the fork (DFS 4% on connected components; a 12-point pass cost and no gain on minimum spanning tree).

  **The boundary units.** The grid path task on Qwen3-8B failed validation (no token at index 3 gives at least 5 of 10 off-default programs), so it joined shortest path and kth smallest as a boundary unit, where a window of 16 body tokens at T 7 over the top 20 replaced the fork dose (Table 387). All three windows fall below the committed pass-rate floor of 0.5, so the test is untestable by breakage. On kth smallest the surviving programs scatter across the catalogue, an effect on the program's form rather than a located choice.

  **Table 387.** The boundary units under a window of 16 tokens at T 7.

  | Task (Qwen3-8B) | Twin | Window | Pass, twin to window | Flips |
  |-|-|-|-|-|
  | Grid path | BFS 0.98, DFS 0.02 | BFS 0.94, DFS 0.02, other 0.04 | 0.88 to 0.20 | 2 |
  | Shortest path | Dijkstra 0.98, Bellman-Ford/SPFA 0.02 | Dijkstra 0.98, Bellman-Ford/SPFA 0.02 | 1.00 to 0.42 | 0 |
  | Kth smallest | Full sort 1.00 | Full sort 0.30, quickselect 0.14, size k heap 0.06, heapify and pop 0.02, counting sort 0.06, other 0.06, invalid 0.36 | 1.00 to 0.24 | 35 |

  **The blind locator.** Prefix resampling at T 1 used 6 base paths per unit, prefixes 2 to 64 and 8 continuations each (3,072 continuations in 16 GPU minutes), with the Bayesian change-point rule of iteration 7. It located minimum spanning tree's fork exactly at token 61 on the three paths that show a change point. The other three show none, one short of the preregistered 4 of 6, because a Kruskal path starts near a 0.65 share of its own class and the share-jump rule cannot fire on it. On connected components no path shows a change point: the twin writes union-find in 50 of 50 programs and resampling at T 1 never leaves it, so the fork at tokens 10 and 11 was known only from iteration 7's pushed and banned prompts. On a collapsed task the knob needs knowledge that a locator at T 1 cannot supply. The opening classifier that stops continuations agrees with the full labels on 0.989 and 0.985 of completed programs.

  **The reachability claim.** At every fork node, each of the 64 most probable tokens was forced and continued five times at T 1; an idea counts when at least one forced continuation is a correct program of it (Table 388). Forcing adds one known idea on three units, as predicted: BFS on connected components, Prim with an array scan on minimum spanning tree weight, and a scan over the alphabet on valid anagram. Each appears at T 1 about once in 2 million to 50 million samples, and the fork dose lifts its mass to at most 0.010, far below the 0.05 the plan asked for, because these ideas sit at deep ranks (ranks 34 and 52 on minimum spanning tree weight, rank 18 on valid anagram) or behind a token whose programs mostly fail (' def bfs' on connected components, whose mapped continuations pass 2 of 10).

  **Geometry at the fork and novelty.** The engine stored the final-norm hidden states of the 16 positions from the fork on, and the artifact plots their first two principal components (61% to 81% of the variance) in actual activation coordinates. The states separate by the algorithm the program implements, and a nearest-centroid check with centroids from the class-forced slots assigns the fork-dosed slots to their own program's class at 0.90 on connected components (94 slots), 0.97 on minimum spanning tree weight (73), 0.975 on trapped rain water (80), 0.83 on valid anagram (77) and 0.69 in Gemma (86), where BFS and DFS programs share most of the opening. The dial reaches the model's own states for its alternative ideas, not new regions. After adjudication only 2 correct programs from any stage carry the label other, both from the kth smallest window and both counting sort in dictionary form; two blind judges (gemini-2.5-flash, 10 of 10 gate controls; deepseek-chat-v3.1, 8 of 10, calling both known controls outside the catalogue novel) and a manual read called both catalogue variants, with nearest known solutions at tree edit distance 35 to 55 among 17,442 solutions. No correct program of 5,543 is novel (rule-of-three upper bound 0.0005).

  ## 8.4 One DAS protocol at the fork of both families (Qwen3-8B and Gemma)

  The DAS experiment  answered the first lead of Section 7.11: the Qwen3-8B and Gemma handles had been tested under different objectives, readouts and permutation schemes, so a matched protocol was part of any test of a variable. One protocol was declared and hash-committed before any GPU use. The map class is a linear orthonormal map of rank 1, 2, 4 or 8 (nested); the interchange adds the map's projection of the source state minus that of the base state; the objective is bounded in the style of CDAS [112], the KL divergence from the source's own class distribution to the edited base's; and the readout is the class margin, the log probability of the source's class minus that of the base's class at the fork. It ran at three sites: the fork of connected components in Qwen3-8B (token 11, after ' def'; classes BFS, DFS and union-find), the fork of Gemma's grid task (token 32; BFS and DFS, because forced A* and IDDFS prompts failed adherence), and Qwen3-8B's task band (blocks 12 to 23 at all 145 task specification positions, one shared map). Seven controls were committed with thresholds before any fit (Table 389). Teacher-forced results are scored on held-out pairs, which need both a held-out source family and a held-out noun; generation is scored by hidden tests on slots of common random numbers.

  **Table 389.** The seven committed controls and their thresholds.

  | Control | What it tests | Pass threshold |
  |-|-|-|
  | Random subspaces | 50 random subspaces per rank | Median recovery at most 0.05 |
  | Label control | Refits on deranged labels (in Gemma, balanced shuffles of two classes) | At most 0.10 of the true fit's effect |
  | Random-initialisation control | The same map class and budget on a randomly initialised network | At most 0.25 of the trained effect |
  | Reverse interchange | Writing the default class's coordinates into a forced base | At least 0.5 of the full-state reverse |
  | Retention | The map projected on the top 64 principal components of natural twin states | At least 0.5 of the effect kept |
  | Natural-variance share | Share of natural twin variance in the subspace | Above the 95th percentile of random subspaces |
  | Seed stability | Principal angles between seeds | Median first cosine at least 0.5 and above the random 99th percentile |

  **Where the decision is written.** Exchanging the full residual state at the fork does almost nothing up to block 14 in either model (under 0.5 nats), so the choice is not yet written into the fork position there. The committed scan rule takes the block that maximises recovery normalised by the full-state effect, and it chose block 22 in Qwen3-8B (full-state effect 1.5 nats) and block 16 in Gemma (2.7 nats), the first blocks where the full state starts to carry the class. A rank-1 subspace there moves the margin 7.9 times (Qwen3-8B) and 2.5 times (Gemma) as much as the full state. A DAS edit that moves the margin far more than exchanging the whole state ever does raises the committed off-manifold flag, the signature of an edit that writes states the model does not produce, as Makelov et al. describe [122]. From block 24 in Qwen3-8B and block 22 in Gemma on, the full-state exchange carries 15 to 25 and 7 to 9 nats, and a rank-1 subspace recovers 0.6 to 0.9 and 1.2 to 1.4 of it. Iteration 7's Gemma block 17 sat on the same weak-ceiling edge.

  The label controls on connected components used two cyclic derangements and a derangement at the prompt level, changing every retained target; they still move held-out pairs toward the true source class, and the first of them also fits its permuted targets (training KL 0.0002) and writes DFS for BFS sources in generation (20 of 20). Gemma's two-class site could only use balanced shuffles that change 33% to 58% of labels, a weaker control, so the matched claim carries the qualifier "three-class label control tested in Qwen3-8B only". The randomly initialised networks have next-token entropies of 11.1 to 12.0 nats, and the full-state exchange on them does little (1.2 and 0.45 nats), yet a linear map at the fork recovers 0.41 to 0.69 of the trained effect: a linear map at one token can manufacture most of the effect with no trained computation behind it, the concern Sutter et al. raise for non-linear maps [132].

  [FIGURE:fig_das_controls]

  **Verdict.** The committed rule confirms the matched DAS claim if both forks are certified and disconfirms it if a fork fails the label control or the random-initialisation control in either family. Both forks fail both, so the claim is disconfirmed; the largest one-sided p over sites of the pair-level tests that the true and trained fits beat their controls is 0.037, so the fits do beat their controls, but by margins far below the committed thresholds. The committed prediction (both forks certified; the band passes generation but fails the reverse, retention and clamp tests) was wrong on both forks and on the band's reverse test. What the protocol finds is a rank-4 edit at the fork that moves the written algorithm in both families, not a certified variable: a certified variable would pass every control. Under the committed rule it is a sufficient handle in Gemma and NO HANDLE at Qwen3-8B's fork, where the edit toward BFS writes BFS in 29 of 30 programs but 24 fail (pass 0.20 against 0.83; 5:0 against random, p 0.063). Neither passes the specificity controls (iteration-9 correction).

  Three readings follow. First, a rank-4 edit at one token moves the algorithm: 29 of 30 correct DFS programs on connected components where the twin writes union-find, and 22 of 30 correct BFS programs in Gemma against 6 unedited and 5 for a random subspace. Second, the edit toward BFS in Qwen3-8B writes the fork token and BFS in 29 of 30 programs, but 24 of them fail; a typical failure returns `len(visited)` from the helper while the caller does `visited.update(bfs(i))`. The model's program around the written token is incoherent, one more sign of an edit off the natural states. Third, no edit restores the default: neither the reverse DAS edit nor the reverse full-state exchange returns a forced prompt to its twin's class in generation (0 of 20 in each cell), because with the opening prefilled through ' def' a forced prompt keeps its class whatever is written at the fork. The band's map toward DFS writes BFS in 24 of 30 programs, and its label-control map writes DFS for both source classes: the rank-2 band handle encodes "leave union-find, toward the algorithm this map was fitted to favour" rather than the source's class, which is the generation face of the label-control failure. A full-state exchange over the band flips the teacher-forced class on only 58% of held-out pairs, below the planned 90%, with positions verified by tests, and the first principal cosines between this band handle and iteration 7's handle are 0.12 to 0.17.

  **Do iteration 4's random pushes act through the fitted subspaces? No.** The 40 random directions of iteration 4 (alpha 2, absolute unit, blocks 12 to 23 at the task specification positions) were projected on the band subspace, and the projection, scaled by the forced-class displacement, was committed as the predictor of each direction's correct off-default share before any outcome was read. The retrospective association is Spearman 0.39 (p 0.006, n 40; 0.36 and 0.39 for the two engines; partial correlation controlling the push norm 0.42 over the band and 0.39 at block 35; a permuted predictor gives 0.14), below the committed 0.5. On 24 prospective directions committed in advance it falls to 0.09 (p 0.33; 208 of 240 programs ran before the time cap). Clamping the subspaces removes nothing (Table 393), so the committed clamp test fails: random pushes move the algorithm through other directions than the fitted handles.

Class centroids are sized by implemented, test-passing programs (connected components: union-find 87, DFS 35, BFS 34; Gemma: DFS 21, BFS 7).   **The post hoc fit at block 24.** Block 24 is the first block where the full-state exchange carries the class in Qwen3-8B (16.2 nats, flipping every held-out pair). The same protocol there, reported as a sensitivity and never substituted for the committed block, recovers 1.22 (0.98 to 1.43), below the off-manifold line, and passes the reverse interchange (1.17), retention (0.52; 0.74 with forced prompts in the basis), natural variance (0.0075 against 0.0010) and seed stability (0.61 to 0.63). The label controls still reach 0.61, 0.57 and 0.50 of the true fit (p 0.0005 each for true above permuted), the randomly initialised network reaches 0.54, and a difference-in-means direction recovers 0.88 to 0.99 and the top four principal components 0.99, the same as DAS. Once the site has a real full-state ceiling, the dormancy and off-manifold failures go away and the lack of specificity stays: the class information at the fork is carried by the natural difference-in-means direction, which a linear map of almost any labelling partly recovers.

  **Novelty, inputs and departures.** None of 1,857 correct programs (1,708 on connected components, 149 in Gemma) is labelled other, so no judge was called (rule-of-three bound 0.0016); 19 Gemma programs are disputed (18 with runtime IDDFS against AST BFS, all failing) and count as neither class. The 20 new single-token twin nouns came from the concreteness norms of the run's dataset dependency, and 76 connected components programs from four of its code datasets served as the nearest known solutions. The run used one 23 GB GPU (Table 374) for about 5.5 hours in all. Minimum spanning tree weight and Gemma's task band were dropped at the first commit, and band fits ran 109 steps with 2 seeds instead of 3. Blocks whose full-state exchange moved fewer than 10% of pairs by 1 nat (blocks 0 to 14) were recorded as undefined. Three stages were rerun, after a NaN-ordering bug, a crash in the two-class label control and an out-of-memory stop. The engine check against iterations 6 and 7 and the band geometry figure were not run, labeller disagreements were not sent to the blind judge, and mediation ran 270 of 300 clamp slots and 208 of 240 prospective programs before the time caps. Eight commits form a chain with no break, and a standard-library re-derivation reproduces all 38 checked headline numbers from the raw rows, with placebos that fail as they should.

  **Positioning.** DAS [110] and Boundless DAS [111] use the same map class; CDAS supplies the bounded objective and the bidirectional test [112]; MIB ranks DAS above difference in means and PCA under teacher forcing but scores no specificity control [52]. Makelov et al. predict the off-manifold overshoot, the failed retention and the failed reverse at the forks [122], Grant et al. describe the divergent representations that interventions produce [141], and Sutter et al. show that maps of enough capacity fit untrained networks [132]. This run adds the full set of specificity controls under one protocol in two families, and the result that even a linear map at the fork fails them.

  ## 8.5 The circuit behind Qwen3-8B's fork

  The circuit experiment  asked which components of Qwen3-8B compute the odds at the fork, and whether steering them rewrites the algorithm in generated, hidden-test-checked programs. It ported iteration 7's Gemma pipeline so that both families are measured the same way. A screen by attribution patching [136] covers 4,752 nodes: 32 heads and one MLP in each of 36 layers, at four position classes (the condition span, the task specification, the shared opening and the fork position). The top nodes are then patched exactly, by noising and denoising, and path patching [135] runs among the top 15, followed by faithfulness curves. Each top-10 node is validated in the real model against 50 matched random components of the same type and position class with matched write norm, under ablation and under steering (exact sign-flip tests, Holm over all 20 node and test p-values). The top five nodes are then steered in generation (30 slots of common random numbers, hidden tests, exact McNemar against a matched random five and against the twin), and a committed motif test compares the circuit with Gemma's. Two contrasts were studied. On minimum spanning tree weight the metric is the logit of ' Kr' minus the logit of ' Prim' after the 61-token opening; on connected components it is ' find' minus ' dfs' after ' def'.

  **The primary contrast changed before any screen row.** The natural contrast on minimum spanning tree weight paired 24 neutral-noun variants per template (nouns from the concreteness norms of the dataset dependency), the variant with the highest metric against the lowest; its mean total effect was 0.89 nats, below 1 nat, which triggered the preregistered fallback: forced-Prim paraphrases against their padding twins became the primary contrast, committed as an amendment before any screen row. On connected components the corrupt run exchanges the forced-DFS prompt's residual states into the twin at every task specification position of all 36 blocks, which flips the teacher-forced argmax to ' dfs' in every pair; because that corruption is an intervention, condition-span nodes have zero effect there by construction, and the contrast maps routing from the task specification to the fork. Table 401 gives the shares. The committed comparison, Qwen3-8B's mixed set against Gemma, reads "different motif" on the condition share and the depth of the fork stack. The committed composition depends on the attribution screen, which missed Qwen3-8B's largest node; with the exhaustive sweep, the condition share of the primary contrast rises to 0.17, still below Gemma's band [0.21, 0.51], and every minimum spanning tree row keeps a fork-stack depth of 0.86 to 0.96, above the band [0.45, 0.80] (the bands are constants of the committed motif code, `src/k3motif.py` line 55), so the post hoc sweep does not turn the committed different-motif reading into a match (iteration-9 correction). What the two families share is a late stack of fork-position MLPs and heads that carries the fork logit, deeper in Qwen3-8B (effect-weighted depth about 0.86 against 0.69); the layer-0 MLP at the condition span carries much of the forced contrast on the 20 pair prompts, but its held-out edit was never applied (see the paragraph after Table 395), and a structural likeness or difference between discovered circuits is not by itself a likeness or difference of mechanism, the phantom specialization that Bayat Makou et al. describe [146].   **Checks and departures.** CPU tests (positions, node keys, the motif on Gemma, sign-flip against brute force, Holm and McNemar against standard libraries, the random-pool ladder, the labeller) all pass; the labeller re-check passes 4 of 4 references per task, 22 of 22 gold rows and 30 of 30 iteration-7 programs. The probability of ' Kr' on the first twin template is 0.724, against 0.72 in iteration 7, and labels agree with the iteration-7 engine on 20 of 20 slots per task (11 of 20 token-identical on minimum spanning tree weight). The metric was read in fp32 from the final-norm state after the first GPU tests showed that bf16 logits are quantised to 0.125 to 0.25 nats at these magnitudes; suffix forwards with a reused prefix cache differ from full recomputation by bf16 path noise (mean 0.076 nats, against 0.061 nats between full forwards in two batch shapes), so every effect is measured against an unedited row of its own batch. The transcoder attribution graph was dropped at the precheck, because Qwen3-8B's per-layer transcoders (about 96.5 GB) exceed both the 23 GB GPU and the 57 GB of RAM, so no feature-level account exists. A second contrast of a ban against the twin on connected components was not run, three natural pairs with total effects below 0.2 nats were dropped from the disjoint set, two out-of-memory stops were resumed from files without dropping rows, and one GPU test (path patching against direct logit attribution) was not run. Of 395 correct generated programs, none is labelled other (rule-of-three bound 0.0076). The nine-link hash chain orders every validation row after its commit and every steered program after its commit.

  ## 8.6 A fair test of Gemma's dial: prompting under matched conditioning, free generation and dormancy

  Iteration 7 found a rank-4 DAS subspace at block 17 of gemma-3-4b-it that, edited once at the fork after the shared 32-token opening, raised correct BFS programs on the grid task from 11 of 50 to 42 of 50, and it compared this with a forced-BFS prompt sampled without that opening (35 of 50). The Gemma experiment  ran the missing cells on the same 50 slots (five templates by ten streams, iteration 7's streams; T 1.0, top-p 1, at most 1,024 new tokens), giving the 2x2 of {prompt, dial} by {opening prefilled, free generation}. It added a dial applied in free generation at the fork's position in each free sample, placed by a rule committed in advance, and ran the dormancy checks at ranks 1, 2, 4 and 8 under the rule already applied to Qwen3-8B. One model, one task and one fork: every claim below holds at Gemma's grid fork.

  **Why prompting fails under the prefill.** The committed prediction that the forced prompt with the opening prefilled would reach at least 40 of 50 correct BFS programs failed completely: it writes BFS 50 of 50 times and every program fails. The prefilled opening is unlikely under the forced prompt: its log probability is -11.3 to -14.1 nats under the five forced-BFS wordings (1e-6 to 1e-5), against -0.11 to -0.17 nats (0.85 to 0.90) under the twins and the forced-DFS prompts. Forcing it drives the fork token to ' queue' (probability 0.96 to 0.998 for all five wordings, 50 of 50 programs), and that opening writes a list-based BFS that carries the path, `queue = [(start, [start])]`, without checking whether start or goal is a wall. Every such program fails the hidden case of a one-by-one wall with a wrong answer, not a timeout, which corrects iteration 7's explanation that the 0 of 125 ' queue' programs failed by slowness. The teacher-forced account of the fork predicted this before any sample: 1.0 correct and 49.97 attempted BFS programs of 50. In free generation the forced prompt never writes the shared opening (index 32 is '[' inside `from collections import deque` in 46 of 50 programs), and the forced-DFS prompt with the opening prefilled is natural and gives 50 of 50 correct DFS. So the prefill is a confound, but it hurts the prompt, not the dial: under matched prefill the dial beats prompting 39 to 0.

  **The dial in free generation.** The rule that places the edit was committed before any edited sample. If the free twin reproduces the shared opening, the edit goes at index 32. Otherwise it goes at the first index from 8 to 96 after the body indent where BFS and DFS together hold at least half the probability, ' visited' holds at least 0.01, and no string naming an algorithm has appeared. 47 of 50 slots reproduce the opening and 3 never reach a qualifying position (73 and 7 over 80 slots with the held-out set); the literal rule of the plan would have fired at index 2 in every slot, as anticipated. No edited row differs from the free twin before the edit (0 of 480), and the edit's decode-time margin at index 32 is 0.42 nats above the prefilled path (12.09 against 11.67 on the first template), above the 0.3 tolerance; the prefilled and decoded paths agree on labels in 46 of 47 dial slots and 42 of 47 twin slots, one slot short of the committed 0.90 for the twin.

  **In free generation the dial does not beat prompting.** Against the committed free prompt (32 of 50) the dial's advantage is 11 to 5 discordant slots (p 0.21). This matches the prior from AxBench that prompting beats steering [34]. The slot-bootstrap interaction, (dial minus prompt, prefilled) minus (dial minus prompt, free), is 0.66 (0.50 to 0.82).

  **Dormancy.** By the committed rule shared with Qwen3-8B, the block-17 subspace is a dormant or off-manifold handle at every rank (Table 406); dormant means that the subspace lies in directions the model's natural states barely use, so that an edit there writes a state the model would not produce on its own. The flag comes through the retention arm alone: projected on the top 64 principal components of the twins' natural fork states, the subspace keeps 0.28, 0.23, 0.21 and 0.18 of its effect at ranks 1, 2, 4 and 8, while the residual orthogonal to them keeps 0.51 to 0.55. The reverse arm does not flag: with forced-BFS bases and twin sources, reverse recovery is 1.53 to 2.39, Haar random subspaces give about 0, and DAS sits at the 100th percentile. The DAS reverse moves the margin -5.58 nats at rank 4, more than the same-site full-state reverse (-2.62); a late-band reverse replacing blocks 17 to 33 moves it -10.4, and DAS is 0.54 of that. Natural variance is low at ranks 1, 2 and 4, as iteration 7 found (reproduced on its cached states to 1.1e-9), and above the random 95th percentile at rank 8. The flag is specific to a natural set of twins only: with the 40 forced sources added, retention rises to 0.62, 0.53, 0.46 and 0.39, the orthogonal residual carries nothing, and the variance share is about 50 times the random 95th percentile. The subspace is almost unused by the twins' own noun-driven variation, but it lies inside the variation that prompts induce. The account's prediction (reverse at least 0.5 and retention at least 0.5 at rank 4) fails on retention. Reverse generation (N 30) is undefined: replacing even the whole block-17 fork state restores 0 DFS programs, and all 30 programs in both reverse cells still take ' queue'.

  **What the subspace carries.** An exploratory layer sweep, committed before its rows, separates the algorithm from the forced prompt's implementation. Transplanting the forced-BFS fork state into the twin at a single block sets the probability of ' queue' to 0.06 to 0.09 up to block 14, 0.43 at block 15, 0.55 at block 17 and 0.94 to 0.98 from block 26. In the other direction, the twin's state written into the forced prompt leaves ' queue' at 0.96 to 0.99 up to block 21, and it falls only from block 22 (0.88; 0.79 at block 24, 0.34 at 26, 0.06 at 33). The block-17 dial reaches the same BFS margin (about 12 nats) with ' queue' at only 0.006 to 0.07, its BFS mass sitting on a blank line and 'if', the openings that check walls first; a difference-in-means edit at the same margin puts 0.94 to 0.98 on ' queue' and destroys the programs (0 of 50 correct, pass 0.00). The subspace moves the algorithm, BFS against DFS, but not the forced prompt's choice of implementation.

  **The dial's geometry (iteration-9 correction).** The Gemma experiment's block-17 geometry figure plots Gemma's block-17 fork states in actual activation coordinates: the 120 twin variants (coloured by fork margin), the forced-BFS and forced-DFS sources, the free twin at its decision position, and the same free-twin states after the rank-4 DAS edit toward BFS or DFS and after the difference-in-means edit toward BFS. In the DAS plane the twin states form one tight cluster; the DAS edits carry them onto the forced-BFS or forced-DFS sources, while the difference-in-means edit throws them far beyond every natural state. In the twins' own first two principal components the DAS-edited states stay inside the twin columns and the difference-in-means states leave them. This is the retention picture of Table 406: a subspace that the twins' noun-driven variation barely uses but that prompts use, and an edit along it that stays near the natural states where the difference-in-means edit does not.

  **Engine, labels, audit and departures.** On an RTX 4090 against iteration 7's RTX 2000 Ada, the prefilled twin gives 10 of 50 (iteration 7: 11) with label agreement 0.94, below 0.95 (kernel sensitivity; every contrast stays inside this engine), the prefilled dial 39 (42) with agreement 1.00, and the free forced prompt 32 (35) with agreement 1.00; recomputed fork states differ from iteration 7's by up to 1.3% in norm (0.73 nats of margin). The frozen labeller labelled 1,320 programs, runtime and AST agree on 1,254, and a blind judge (gpt-4.1-mini, mostly from iteration 7's cache) settled the other 66; a blind re-gate agrees 30 of 30 with the labeller, and no program was truncated or labelled other. None of 913 correct programs is novel (rule-of-three bound 0.0033). A standard-library audit re-derives 139 quantities from the labels with 0 mismatches, an independent re-scoring of the 8 headline cells from raw text with its own test runner and classifier agrees on 400 of 400 programs and reproduces every headline test and the interaction, and within-slot permutation placebos give p below 0.05 in 0% to 3.1% of 1,000 permutations. Generation used DAS seed 0, class targets at ranks up to 4 came from iteration 7's commit, the decision rule was refined as described, the stage that pools known solutions was rebuilt in the novelty stage (2,158 graph, grid and path programs from 7 code datasets), and DAS refits and the label and random-initialisation controls were not re-run, so iteration 7's passed controls stand. Spend was USD 0.0042 and about 14 GPU minutes.

  **Positioning.** CDAS already validates DAS-based steering by generation and compares it with prompting [112], and prefix steering shows that an intervention over a short span, even one token, retains much of full steering's control [140]. What this experiment adds is a causally localised subspace edited at a decision position read off the model's own trajectory, prompting cells matched to its prefill on the same slots, hidden-test correctness, and the dormancy and implementation-channel analysis. The permitted wording is: at Gemma's grid fork, a one-shot DAS edit at the fork works in free generation as it does after a prefill; prompting under the prefill fails because the prefill is off-policy for the prompt; in free generation the dial lies within the range of prompt wordings.

  ## 8.7 A temperature law composed over forks, tested on held-out families

  Section 7.5 found on Qwen3-8B that dividing the fork logits by T predicted the temperature response on one unit of three. The temperature-law experiment  turned this into a preregistered test across three families, with held-out units on which the law was never developed. For each unit (a task on one model) the pipeline found the forks blind: prefix resampling along stratified base programs, a preregistered Bayesian change-point rule, single-token refinement, and forced-token confirmation, with a second fork searched inside any branch whose algorithm stays impure. It then committed, by hash and before any temperature sample, the law's prediction of the attempted-label distribution at T 0.3, 0.7, 1.0 and 1.3 under top-p 1 and top-k 10, computed only from teacher-forced logits along the openings and at the forks and from the T 1 conditionals of the algorithm given each fork token. We call this the *composed law*: the share of each algorithm is the probability of each opening at temperature T, times the tempered distribution of the fork token given the opening, times the probability of the algorithm given that token, where a token followed by a second fork contributes the same mixture over the second fork's tokens. Four rivals were committed with it: a flat law (the fit twin's shares at every T), algorithm-level tempering (the twin's shares raised to the power 1/T and renormalised), a single-fork law without the second level, and the same law at the highest-entropy position. The same 100 fresh random streams were sampled at every temperature, and each predictor is scored by its mean absolute error, the mean over temperatures of the total variation distance between predicted and observed label distributions. A unit passes at a mean absolute error of at most 0.10 with the entropy of the algorithm given the fork classes at most 0.3 bits; the claim passes on at least 70% of scored units including at least 3 held-out units, with at least 4 scored.

  The units were three Qwen3-8B tasks used to develop the law (trapped rain water, valid anagram, minimum spanning tree weight), two held-out Gemma tasks (substring search and first and last position in a sorted array) and one held-out Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct task (the grid path). The two Llama bench units selected from its pilot (kth smallest and find duplicate) were dropped under the plan's time box.

  **The held-out Gemma units pass, and the second level matters.** On substring search the blind locator puts the fork right after `if len(needle) > len(haystack): return -1`, and the law's error is 0.033. On first and last position the first fork, 'first', is impure, so the second-fork search ran inside it and found token 24; with it the law's error is 0.014, against 0.051 for the same law without the second level (bootstrap 95% CI of the difference -0.051 to -0.011) and 0.073 for the flat law. On both Gemma units the drop from T 1.0 to 0.3 is one-directional (10:0 and 13:0).

  **The development units pass, and iteration 7's misses do not recur.** On trapped rain water the locator rebuilt iteration 7's structure blind: two 18-token openings, ' n' (0.80) to the arrays and ' left' (0.20, or 0.62 in the second cluster) mostly to two pointers, with the second fork at token 19 separating ' left =' from ' left_max'. Iteration 7's error of 0.105 on 50 streams falls to 0.029 on 100 fresh streams. On minimum spanning tree weight the fresh-stream Prim share at T 1.0 is 25 of 100 against a prediction of 0.231 (binomial p 0.64), against iteration 7's 20 of 50 (Fisher p 0.09) and its twin's 19 of 100 (p 0.39): the lean that iteration 7 attributed to its streams was a property of those streams. Valid anagram passes, but the flat law beats the composed law (0.030 against 0.054); as in iteration 7, temperature barely moves this unit.

  **The held-out Llama unit fails, for a reason outside the law's scope.** Llama's opening classifier failed its gate (the frozen labeller calls some path-storing BFS programs IDDFS), so every locator continuation was completed and labelled (3,276 continuations, on a grid thinned by the plan's cost rule). The locator found forks of the same kind as Gemma's, but Llama reaches them through many openings: the two confirmed openings cover about 2% of the fit twin, so the committed law is almost the twin's flat shares, and the entropy of the algorithm given the fork classes is 0.63 bits, above the 0.3 criterion. Observed BFS is 0.76, 0.66 and 0.61 and DFS 0.12, 0.24 and 0.21 at T 0.3, 0.7 and 1.0. At T 1.3 the programs degenerate: 72 of 100 run to the 1,536-token cap, the pass rate falls to 0.04, and the frozen labeller calls 87 of them other; that cell exceeded the preregistered 20% bar for other and was adjudicated by two judge families with a tiebreak (43 BFS, 15 DFS, 29 other), and the adjudicated column is primary (BFS 0.53, DFS 0.16, other 0.29). Every predictor fails on this unit (0.134 to 0.143; 0.28 to 0.29 with the frozen labels): no algorithm-level law predicts the collapse into unusable programs. Llama's top-k cells, built by keeping each top-p program up to its first token outside the top 10 and regenerating from there (shadow sampling), were reported but not used, because the construction failed its validation (1 of 20 directly sampled programs at T 1.3 token-identical).

  **Verdict and rivals.** Five of six scored units pass (0.83, above 0.70), including both held-out Gemma units, but only 3 held-out units were scored where the claim needs at least 4, so the verdict is partial: the held-out criterion is underpowered, not met, and no held-out unit exceeds 0.2, so the disconfirming branch does not fire. The composed law has the lowest error on 3 of 6 units and beats the flat law on 4 of 6, tempering on 5 of 6, the highest-entropy rival on 5 of 6 and the single-fork law on 3 of 6, equalling it where no second fork exists; the exact one-sided sign test of the law against the flat law over units gives p 0.34. Slot-bootstrap 95% intervals of the error difference against the flat law exclude 0 on minimum spanning tree weight [-0.050, -0.025], first and last position [-0.081, -0.018] and substring search [-0.041, -0.002]. Algorithm-level tempering is a strong rival: it beats the law on substring search (0.023 against 0.033) and comes close on first and last position and minimum spanning tree weight, so much of the temperature response is sharpening or flattening the known mix. The law adds most where an impure first fork needs the second level (first and last position, trapped rain water) and where the default is not the share being sharpened (minimum spanning tree weight). Three placebos behave as they should. Permuting the predictions across temperatures puts the true error below the 5th percentile on trapped rain water, minimum spanning tree weight and first and last position (not on the two nearly flat units nor on Llama). Shuffling the conditional of the algorithm given the token across tokens raises the error (p at most 0.02 on four units, 0.10 on substring search). Shuffling temperature labels within slots rejects the drop test at the nominal rate (0.02 to 0.04). Replaying each slot's own uniforms through the committed token classes names the algorithm of 0.87 to 0.99 of Qwen3-8B slots on the opening (0.94 to 1.00 in Gemma), and the replay-implied shares lie within 0.00 to 0.04 of the observed cells on every passing unit, so the remaining error is the law's expectation against 100 realised streams.

  **Is the instruct model's fork the base model's mean answer?** Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-8B-Base were teacher-forced on identical chat-templated ids at the forks and at 64 phrasing positions of 20 programs per task (Table 410). On the three collapsed tasks, post-training widened the fork margin by 2.11 to 13.41 nats while the entropy at phrasing positions moved by less than 0.5 nats (0.23 to 0.31; the base model is uniformly a little less certain), as committed; without chat tokens the gains are 2.69 to 11.05, so the result is not an artefact of the template. The Jensen-Shannon divergence between the two models is 6 to 10 times larger at the fork than at phrasing positions, and 1.5 to 1.9 times larger than at phrasing positions of the same base-entropy decile on the collapsed tasks (equal on minimum spanning tree weight, lower on trapped rain water); random positions show no excess. At phrasing positions the instruct token is the base model's top token at 89% to 95% of positions (the URIAL token categories [100]), but at the fork it is mostly the base model's second or third choice. The instruct default is therefore not the base model's mean (that post-training shifts concentrate at the base model's high-entropy forks is already shown by Cantarero et al. [142] and Sparse but Critical [143]; what this sub-arm adds is the algorithm-level outcome on code at a counterfactually located fork) (iteration-9 correction): on minimum spanning tree weight the base model's fork distribution, pushed through the instruct model's conditional of the algorithm given each token, would give Prim 0.68 where the instruct model writes Kruskal 0.78; on trapped rain water, two pointers 0.37 against 0.29. Post-training moved and sharpened one token; the repertoire of ideas stayed the same.

  **Ideas against phrasings (question 1a-c of the request).** Across 4,800 sweep programs no unit produced an algorithm outside its catalogue at any temperature. At T 0.3 each sweep is essentially one idea with one to four phrasing clusters (identifier-normalised AST 4-gram Jaccard 0.8): first and last position 100 linear scans in 2 clusters; minimum spanning tree weight 93 Kruskal in 4 clusters and 7 Prim in 2; trapped rain water 83 array programs in 1 cluster and 17 two-pointer programs in 1. Loosening T does not add ideas; it moves mass to the second known idea at the predicted rate and multiplies its phrasings: at T 1.3 minimum spanning tree weight has 66 Kruskal programs in 22 clusters and 31 Prim in 7, and first and last position 76 linear scans in 2 clusters and 24 binary searches in 8. Correct-only Hill-1 rises accordingly (1.29 to 2.06 and 1.00 to 1.68). Top-k 10 is token-identical to top-p 1 on every Qwen3-8B and Gemma cell except 6 of minimum spanning tree weight's 400 programs, which were regenerated after a divergence. The novelty audit read every correct program labelled outside the catalogue (10 distinct among 4,703 correct programs, checked against an 18,305-solution corpus built from the dataset dependency plus references, with two judge families passing 3 of 3 known-class controls and a manual read): 8 labeller misses of catalogue algorithms, 1 catalogue variant and 1 known brute force outside the catalogue; none is novel (rule-of-three bound 0.0006).

  **Validity checks and departures.** The hash chain verifies end to end, with each family's forks and predictions committed before any sweep sample of that family and four amendments (the adjudication rule, a locator fix for nested openings, content-addressed continuation ids, and a predictor fix for second forks not found) committed before the samples they govern; the held-out families' predictions were committed and swept before any Qwen3-8B sample. CPU tests pass, including a two-level tree exact to 1e-9 and top-k shadow sampling equal to direct top-k on 1,000 synthetic sequences; the change-point rule has a 0.00 false-positive rate on 200 null series and 0.865 power on planted jumps; the scoring code reproduces iteration 7's errors exactly (0.083, 0.105 and 0.043). Gemma prompt ids reproduce earlier hashes on all 10 templates, sweep streams are disjoint from every earlier key (0 overlaps among 1,300 seeds), and per-slot labels agree with earlier engines on 0.92 (trapped rain water, below the 0.95 expectation), 0.95 and 0.98 of Qwen3-8B slots and 0.98 and 0.97 of Gemma slots. Llama's bf16 twin on the grid (BFS 60, DFS 23, IDDFS 14, other 3) differs from iteration 2's twin, served by vLLM with 8-bit floating-point weights (BFS 77, DFS 20, other 3; Fisher p 0.015 on BFS), so every Llama contrast stays within this engine. The Llama label re-gate was weak (agreement 0.10 and 0.71 on the two bench units), so primary scoring stays on the frozen labeller with the judge-adjudicated labels as a sensitivity. The base sub-arm used the 20 stored iteration-7 programs for its three collapsed tasks, and frozen-labeller disputed labels count as other. Spend was USD 0.046.

  ## 8.8 The top-five prohibition across ten configurations, and where the survivors land

  The request asks what happens when a model's five most used algorithms are prohibited: do the survivors come from the edge of the banned set or from its opposite side? Earlier iterations found that Qwen3-8B (iteration 2) and gemma-3-4b-it (iteration 6) answer a ban of five names by reimplementing a banned algorithm under another name, so there were no survivors to place. The prohibition experiment  first screened eight new open configurations plus two carried rows for one that obeys, then placed that model's survivors on its own manifold of ten forced algorithms, in actual activation coordinates; each forced prompt names its algorithm by one of three aliases, so the manifold is alias-named (iteration-9 correction). Each configuration's banned set is its own top five by implemented count, filled from BFS, DFS, greedy best-first, IDDFS and A*; because every baseline wrote only BFS and DFS, the banned set is the same five for every configuration. A correct survivor is a program under the ban that passes the 48-case hidden suite and whose adjudicated mechanism is outside the banned set: a non-banned catalogue algorithm or a named known algorithm outside the catalogue. Four commits fixed the configurations, prompts, selection rule, labelling and adjudication, geometry, landing nulls, robustness rule and the prediction (edge) before the samples they govern.

  [FIGURE:fig_ban_screen]

  **Who obeys.** Almost no open configuration obeys a ban of five names. The committed rule (share at least 0.20) selects one: Qwen3-32B with thinking on, 17 of 50 correct survivors, namely unit-weight Dijkstra 6, Bellman-Ford/SPFA run on the grid 7, a frontier search with random priorities 2, a random walk with restarts 1 and wavefront propagation 1. Thinking is the switch, and size matters: the same 32B weights with thinking off reach 0.08, Qwen3-14B reaches 0.14 with thinking on and 0.00 without, and Qwen3-8B with thinking on reaches 0.00 (it writes BFS 11 and DFS 19 under the ban). Disobedience mostly reimplements a banned mechanism without naming it: among programs that use a banned mechanism, 55% to 100% contain no alias of any banned algorithm in the code, the lesson of iteration 2 now across families. Obeying is expensive: the thinking 32B model's mean reasoning grows from 6,864 to 9,090 tokens under the ban, and 23 of 50 ban answers hit the 9,728-token cap (7 of 100 at baseline), counted as non-survivors. The ban costs correctness elsewhere too: Llama's pass rate falls to 0.02 and Qwen3-8B with thinking on passes 0.13.

  **How robust "obeys" is.** The committed definition counts a correct program as a survivor if its adjudicated mechanism is a non-banned catalogue algorithm or a named known algorithm outside the catalogue. The strictest reading drops every survivor outside the catalogue whose adjudicated name, or any novelty judge's name for it, mentions BFS, DFS or SPFA. It leaves 11 of 50 (0.22) on the screen and 14 of 50 (0.28) on the confirmation, still above the bar. Counting catalogue algorithms only gives 6 of 50 (0.12) and 9 of 50 (0.18), below it. "Obeys" therefore rests on counting genuinely different known algorithms, mostly Bellman-Ford on the grid, as obedience; those programs sit outside the ten-algorithm manifold and are not part of the landing test.

  **The manifold of the model that obeys.** States are residual-stream block outputs of Qwen3-32B, read from a checkpoint whose weights are quantised to 4-bit NormalFloat and averaged over the task specification tokens, for 300 forced prompts (ten algorithms by ten templates by three aliases); the decoder is truncated to 48 of 64 blocks, exact for every block used. Every block from 19 to 45 classifies the forced algorithm perfectly (grouped 10-fold balanced accuracy 1.00, holding out template and alias groups), and the committed ceiling rule chose block 31. There the first two principal components explain 32.4% and 12.0% of the variance; classical MDS has stress-1 0.42 on the 300 points and 0.28 on the ten centroids; and the Isomap neighbour graph has 8, 3 and 1 components at k 5, 10 and 15, so the committed primary k is 15. We write g for an algorithm's geodesic distance to the banned five: the smallest, over the five banned algorithms, of the mean geodesic distance between its points and theirs. A non-banned algorithm is called edge when its g lies below the median g of the five non-banned algorithms, opposite when it lies above that median, and middle at the median; the landing statistic is the mean g over the correct catalogue survivors (Table 412). The manifold is built from 300 prompts that each name the algorithm by one of three aliases, so 'opposite' may reflect the distance between names: every bidirectional BFS alias contains 'BFS' or 'breadth-first', every bidirectional A* alias contains 'A*', IDA*'s aliases contain 'A*', 'iterative deepening' or 'Manhattan heuristic', and jump point search and unit-weight Dijkstra share no algorithm-specific term with any banned alias (iteration-9 correction).

The ten centroids carry no loop (the persistence of their one-dimensional loops, measured by persistent homology, is 0.00 against a 95th percentile of 1.19 for covariance-matched Gaussian clouds), and the 300 points carry little (1.59 against 1.29), so edge and opposite are classes of geodesic distance on a manifold that is not a ring and whose prompts name each algorithm by one of three aliases (iteration-9 correction).

  **Landing.** The screen's correct catalogue survivors are 6 of 6 unit-weight Dijkstra, so the landing statistic is 21.59, and the committed verdict is opposite on the alias-named manifold (iteration-9 correction): the preregistered edge prediction is not supported. Under the uniform null and the baseline-frequency null, p for opposite is 0.0001; under a null weighted by how often each algorithm is written correctly when forced (the correctness-filter confound), 0.057; under the exact permutation of algorithm identities, 0.20, which is that null's floor, because one landing algorithm cannot reach significance at the level of algorithms. The attempted-survivor, Euclidean-centroid and standardised-coordinate variants also give opposite. Robustness fails: opposite holds in 10 of 15 cells (every block from 29 to 33 at k 10 and k 15), but at k 5 unit Dijkstra is middle in all five blocks, against a committed bar of 12 of 15.

  **Is 'opposite' a property of the names? (iteration-9 correction)** Each of the 300 forced prompts names its algorithm by one of three aliases, and the aliases of the edge algorithms share words with the banned names. On iteration 8's own stored geodesics at block 31 (every gate passes: the stored labels, prompt groups and algorithm-level g reproduce to 1e-9, and an independent kNN-geodesic recomputation from the stored states correlates with the stored k 15 matrix at 1.000), each non-banned algorithm was split into its three alias sets of 10 prompts and each set's g was computed (unit-weight Dijkstra 18.1 to 24.2, jump point search 14.2 to 18.8, IDA* 11.8 to 15.6, bidirectional A* 11.0 to 12.3, bidirectional BFS 9.2 to 12.4). The lexical overlap was committed by hash before any alias-level number: the number of banned-name detectors an alias matches (0 for every unit-weight Dijkstra and jump point search alias, 1 for every bidirectional BFS and bidirectional A* alias, 1 to 3 for IDA*). Across the 15 alias sets at k 15 the Spearman correlation is -0.61 (exact one-sided p 0.009 over all 360,360 assignments; 95% interval over template resamples -0.71 to -0.59), -0.77 at k 10 (p 0.0007), and -0.77 with content-word overlap. That statistic treats the 15 sets as exchangeable although they are nested in five algorithms, and between algorithms lexical overlap is confounded with mechanism: bidirectional BFS is next to BFS both in name and in mechanism. At the level of algorithms the correlation is -0.63 with p 0.13 (exact over 120 permutations; the tied overlap vector cannot go below 0.033). Holding the algorithm fixed and varying only the name, the within-algorithm test on content-word overlap (3 algorithms whose aliases differ; exact null over 216 distinct relabelings) gives a mean within-algorithm Spearman of -0.12 (p 0.46; p 0.72 at k 10), and the fixed-effects slope of g on overlap is 2.36 (two-sided stratified p 0.78), the wrong sign for a name effect. A sensitivity committed as optional scores overlap with the model's own BPE tokens (function words included, so every algorithm's aliases differ): the 15-set correlation is -0.77, and the within-algorithm statistic is -0.50 (p 0.057 over 7,776 relabelings; -0.40, p 0.11 at k 10), so a small within-algorithm name effect cannot be excluded at this resolution. Placebos fail as they must (at the 0.05 level, shuffled point labels reject in a share 0.048 of draws and random overlap vectors in 0.050) and a planted effect is recovered (rho -0.92, p 3e-06). By the committed wording rule: g follows alias overlap across algorithms (rho -0.61, exact p 0.009), but the pattern is carried by algorithm identity; on this manifold names and mechanisms are confounded, and TP-G's name-free manifolds decide. The planner's expectation of about -0.70 was public before the computation, so only the within-algorithm test and the interval were unseen; tables/alias_g.csv of the Step-0 artifact gives every set.

  **Novelty, audits and departures.** Of 661 correct programs across all arms, 27 were adjudicated other or flagged for a manual read; each was shown to two blind judges with its three nearest known solutions (tree edit distance on normalised ASTs over 1,987 grid and graph search programs). Qwen3-8B's thinking ban arm was cut to its committed floor of 30 because each row took 57 s. Spend was USD 1.53.

  ## 8.9 Comparisons across this iteration's experiments

  **Temperature acts through one or two tokens and only reweights known ideas.** Three experiments measured temperature at the fork from different sides. The fork-dosing experiment predicted the algorithm mix of every dosed cell within a mean absolute error of 0.010 to 0.047 on five units, the temperature-law experiment predicted global temperature sweeps within 0.014 to 0.054 on five of six units, two of them in a held-out family, and both found nothing outside the catalogue; on 5 of 6 units the fork tokens predict temperature's effect on the algorithm mix, but the flat law is better on valid anagram (0.030 against 0.054), algorithm-level tempering is better on substring search (0.023 against 0.033), the law beats the flat law on only 4 of 6 units (sign test p 0.34), and on Llama's grid task every predictor fails (0.142) (iteration-9 correction). Where the twin is already mixed, any knob that reaches the fork does about as well as the dial (min-p on minimum spanning tree weight, global T 1.3 in Gemma); the dial clearly earns its place on valid anagram, where it raises correct-only Hill-1 from 1.78 to 2.78. On the collapsed connected components task it beats every comparator family only after the amendment removed the tokens that break programs (Hill-1 1.54 against 1.17 for the best comparator, lower bound of the difference +0.01), still short of two ideas. Where the twin has collapsed, the fork's top 20 candidates hold at most about 19% for the alternative, so no dose at that token reaches two ideas without breakage. The forced branches show what lies beyond: one known idea per unit on three units, reachable at T 1 once in 2 million to 50 million samples. The base sub-arm explains why: post-training widened the fork margin by 2 to 13 nats on the collapsed tasks while leaving the phrasing positions almost untouched.

  **Internal handles act at the fork, and none is a certified variable.** Table 414 sets the internal results side by side. On connected components three different edits at late fork-position sites all write DFS: the rank-4 DAS map at block 22 (29 of 30 correct toward DFS; toward BFS it writes BFS in 29 of 30 programs but only 5 correct, NO HANDLE by the committed rule) (iteration-9 correction), the top five circuit components at dose 2 (29 of 30) and the matched random five at dose 2 (30 of 30), while a random rank-4 subspace does nothing (0 of 30). The fork margin there is easy to move with a large enough push at the right place, which is why the controls that ask whether the handle is the model's own variable (permuted labels, an untrained network, matched random components) fail or saturate. The circuit separates from random components only at a dose small enough to leave room (24:0 at dose 0.5 on connected components; 6:1 on minimum spanning tree weight). In Gemma the dial is a dormant handle by retention but lies inside the variation prompts induce, works in free generation and ties prompting there.

  **The prohibition answers the request's question on one model.** Only Qwen3-32B with thinking on obeys a five-name ban often enough to place survivors, and its catalogue survivors are all unit-weight Dijkstra, the farthest non-banned algorithm from the banned five, on the screen and on held-out templates. That manifold is built from 300 prompts that each name the algorithm by one of three aliases, and its alias analysis (Section 8.8) finds that g follows alias overlap across algorithms (rho -0.61, exact p 0.009) but not clearly within them (stratified p 0.46 on content words; 0.057 on the model's BPE tokens): names and mechanisms are confounded there, and the name-free manifolds of TP-G decide (iteration-9 correction). The ban prompts themselves move toward two of the banned algorithms, not toward where the survivors land. With one landing algorithm the evidence at the level of algorithms is p 0.20, so the result reads as a description of one model, not a law.
