- iteration: 8
  name: gen_art_experiment_44
  type: experiment
  title: Which open models obey a five-algorithm ban
  summary: |-
    Iteration-8 top-five ban study (gen_plan_experiment_6_idx7) on the T1 grid-path task, with four hash-chained commits in commitments.log.

    SCREEN: 8 new open-model configurations plus 2 carried rows. Each model's own baseline defines its banned set B_c, and for every configuration B_c = {BFS, DFS, IDDFS, A*, greedy best-first}. The literal five-name ban (iteration-2 templates W1-W3) was sampled N=50 per configuration (N=30 for C1).
    - Programs: scored on the 48-case hidden suite (plus the 41-case ITER1 suite) and labelled by the exp9 10-class runtime/AST labeller.
    - Adjudication: gated judges deepseek-chat-v3.1 9/10 and kimi-k2 10/10, third judge mistral-medium-3.1 9/10, plus executor manual reads.
    - Result: only C6, Qwen3-32B thinking on (DeepInfra fp8), clears the committed 0.20 bar, with 17/50 correct survivors = 0.34 (Wilson 0.22-0.48). The survivors are unit Dijkstra 6, Bellman-Ford/SPFA 7, random-priority search 2, random walk 1 and wavefront 1.
    - Others: C4 Qwen3-14B thinking on 0.14; C5 Qwen3-32B thinking off 0.08. Qwen3-8B thinking on (local vLLM FP8), Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-14B thinking off, gemma-3-27b-it, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B and the carried Qwen3-8B thinking off and gemma-3-4b rows are all 0.00.
    - Disobedience: banned BFS/DFS is re-implemented without naming it (55-100% name-free).
    - Cost of obeying: the ban raises C6 reasoning from 6.9k to 9.1k tokens and truncation from 7% to 46%.
    - Strictest reading: dropping BFS/DFS/SPFA-named 'other' survivors leaves C6 at 0.22. Catalogue-only survivors give 0.12.

    GEOMETRY on m* = C6. States come from unsloth/Qwen3-32B-bnb-4bit (nf4) with a truncated decoder (exact): S-mean over task-spec tokens of 300 forced prompts.
    - Layer: every block from 19 to 45 classifies the forced algorithm at CV accuracy 1.00, so L* = 31.
    - Manifold: PCA 32.4%/12.0%; MDS stress-1 0.42 (points) and 0.28 (centroids); Isomap components 8/3/1 at k=5/10/15, so the primary k is 15. Split-half reliability is 0.58/0.95/0.98.
    - Classes: unit Dijkstra is the farthest non-banned algorithm from the banned five (OPPOSITE, bootstrap-stable). Bidirectional BFS and bidirectional A* are EDGE.

    nodes close 1.00 [0.96, 1.04] of the 2.06-nat gap but 50 write-norm-matched random late sets close a median 0.81 (p =
    0.45; R-pure p = 0.039); on CC the stack closes 0.45 [0.28, 0.57] of a 4.52-nat gap vs random median -0.22 (p = 0.020).

    accounts for 43% (MST) / 85% (CC) of the gap (CPU readout decomposition), which is why RS-fork(36) < 1. Committed verdict

  title: Token forcing vs temperature in LLM search for TSP heuristics
  summary: >-
    NOV-T experiment (claim V4): does decision-token branching (DTB: force a rank-2..8 token at the highest-entropy code position
    of the first 48 body tokens, then continue at T 1) make an LLM program search find more distinct heuristic behaviours
    than temperature? Task: constructive TSP with the ReEvo/EoH select_next_node interface; Qwen3-8B-FP8 on vLLM 0.11 (NVIDIA
    L4) mutates programs in a FunSearch-style 5-island search seeded with nearest neighbour (NN); fitness F normalised to
    NN on 64 selection instances (n 50/100) against LKH-3 tours. Arms at matched calls in interleaved rounds: T1.0, T1.6 (top-p
    0.95), DTB, RPB (random-position placebo), IDEA, plus NOSEL (no selection); seeds 0 and 1; 1,056 calls per arm-seed (hard
    stop below the committed C*=2000), 10,812 calls total. Behaviour instrument: next-city decisions on 2,000 frozen probe
    states, complete-linkage clusters at agreement >= 0.95. RESULTS. V2-T DISCONFIRMED by the pre-registered rule: clusters
    per 1,000 calls T1.0 228/234, T1.6 88/104, DTB 228/217, RPB 237/233, IDEA 296/298 (seed 0/1); pooled DTB/T1.0 = 0.963
    (kill condition <= 1.0), DTB/T1.6 = 2.315 (T1.6 validity 0.31-0.32), DTB/RPB = 0.948; per-seed DTB/T1.0 1.00 [0.89,1.14]
    and 0.93 [0.83,1.02] (round-block bootstrap); no sign reversal in secondary (better-than-NN), per-token, rarefied or pooled-linkage
    sensitivities. DTB's held-out best is worse than T1.0's (paired +1.2 and +2.7 gap points). V1-T SUPPORTED: every core
    arm-seed best closes >= 20% of NN's held-out n=200 gap (NN 23.94%, bar 19.15%; bests 13.98-16.68%), confirmed on 96 extra
    n=200 instances and 13 TSPLIB optima. Comparators on the same instances: ReEvo/EoH seed rule 13.67% (no searched program

- iteration: 10
  name: gen_art_experiment_54
  type: experiment
  title: Do banned bin-packing rules come back renamed?
  summary: >-
    NOV-R experiment (plan gen_plan_experiment_4_idx4), 1,143 one-shot online bin-packing priority functions in the exact
    FunSearch interface from Qwen3-8B (no thinking, local vLLM FP8, N 50 per cell), Qwen3-14B and Qwen3-32B (thinking, OpenRouter
    DeepInfra fp8, N 30 per cell after the reduction ladder). Cells: BASE, cumulative name bans of each model's own top-k
    textbook rules (NAME_1..5, templates W1-W3), a described ban (DESC_5), held-out templates (HOLD_5), and two novelty instructions
    (INSTR_NEW, INSTR_LONG). Baseline instrument = lexical compliance L1 (no banned name or abbreviation in the program);
    proposed instrument = mechanistic compliance (exact-decision agreement < 0.95 with every banned rule on 2,000 committed
    probe states, plus a stochastic random-fit matcher), gated beforehand on planted controls (min margin 0.49). Results:
    P1 PARTIAL. The renaming gap appears only without thinking: Qwen3-8B k = 5 gap L1 0.91 vs mechanistic 0.51, +0.40 [0.21,
    0.55] (paired Newcombe), and at k = 1, 14 of 35 lexically clean programs (0.40) are still best fit under another name.
    Qwen3-14B/32B really leave the banned rules (mechanistic 0.93-1.00; gaps +0.04 and -0.13, CIs span 0), and their traces
    name the banned rule in 100% and self-identify near it in 90-100%. Under a BF ban Qwen3-32B switches to first fit in 14/30.
    JT trend p = 0.54 / 0.038 (Holm 0.11) / 0.38; held-out-template gaps are not significant. The verdict is unchanged at
    thresholds 0.90/0.98 and on informative states. P2 DISCONFIRMED: only first fit's description passed the naming check
    (models call the other descriptions 'First Fit Decreasing'), so DESC_5 bans FF only, and compliance is about 1.0 either
    way. P3 SUPPORTED: 0/1,143 programs beat best fit on both held-out sets (FunSearch OR3, Weibull 5k); 186 are behaviourally
    novel vs the 426-member published corpus, but none is better. The novelty instruction 'Make a new algorithm' gives best
    fit in 28/29 (14B) and 28/28 (32B). BASE is almost all best fit for the thinking models (50/50, 48/49). Independent stdlib
    re-derivation (audit/rederive.py): 0 mismatches across agreements, classes, lexical flags, cell counts, JT, both Newcombe
    intervals and the verdicts; all 4 placebos fail as required. Files: method_out.json / full_ / mini_ / preview_ (exp_gen_sol_out:
    novr_samples with predict_mechanism_class, predict_lexical_L1, predict_mechanistic_compliance, predict_valid, predict_better_heldout,
    predict_novel; novr_cells; novr_instrument; metadata with every analysis), data/samples.jsonl (shared schema), data/samples_raw_*.jsonl
    (responses and reasoning), data/decisions.jsonl, results/*.json, figures F1-F6 (including the MDS behaviour map in decision
    space). Caveats: one model family (Qwen3); the container crashed at 4.2 h and sampling resumed at 5.9 h. A duplicate orchestrator
    ran for 40 min: 5 duplicate rows were removed, the naming check was rerun cleanly and committed as commit #3 before the
    DESC_5 rows it governs, and the commit #2 payload files of q14/q32 were overwritten after hashing (chain lines intact;
    B_k identical in every version). Spend USD 1.42.

    /ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_5eGZGmskluur/3_invention_loop/iter_10/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_54

- iteration: 10
  name: gen_art_experiment_55
  type: experiment
  title: Do code-model maps track search order or storage?
  summary: >-
    TP-G2 (iteration 10; continues iteration-9 TP-G art_VVA3P0ocZNA2 / art_8nXdw3_lDAll). Qwen3-32B (OpenRouter, DeepInfra,
    thinking off; 1,138 calls, USD 0.25) wrote name-scrubbed grid path programs for a pre-committed 6x6 discipline x container
    factorial. Prompts named no algorithm (lint 0 hits). Verification: 48- and 41-case suites, AST container checks, tracer/runtime
    discipline checks and 139 executor hand reads. 24 cells, 287 frozen programs (12 per cell, RELAX-SET 11), plus 48 top-ups
    (BiBFS, IDDFS, BiA*, JPS; all JPS and half of BiA* are paraphrases of references). States: iteration 9's frozen readout
    R1 (mean over code tokens) under neutral-twin contexts; Qwen3-8B bf16 block 17 and Qwen3-32B NF4 block 33 via the exact
    truncated decoder; R0 gate reproduced iteration 9 bit for bit. G1 (partial Spearman, 1,000 program bootstraps, 2,000 within-stratum
    permutations): discipline given container rho_dc = 0.226 [0.186, 0.265] on 8B and 0.285 [0.252, 0.321] on 32B. Container
    given discipline is larger: rho_cd = 0.300 and 0.414, delta CI below 0 on both. Crossed 3x4 core: rho_dc 0.280 / 0.336,
    rho_cd 0.366 / 0.545. Baselines: bag-of-tokens E0 0.17 / 0.16; random-init RANDNET 0.07. Rank regression: token surface
    (0.32 / 0.41 semi-partial) and length dominate. Noise ceiling 0.94. Verdict INDETERMINATE: a real discipline signal (p
    = 0.0005, above E0 and RANDNET), but smaller than container and surface. G2 (iteration 9's kNN-geodesic landing on a 464-program
    frame; class LOO 0.68 / 0.83, chance 0.03): covert BFS/DFS programs of the five-name ban land on banned classes 0.99 /
    0.98 (P-COV, 12/12 robustness cells). Grid Bellman-Ford survivors land nearest RELAX cells 30/32 and 31/32; r_F is OPPOSITE
    on 32B and EDGE on 8B (P-BF met 8/12). Unit-weight Dijkstra lands nearest COST-HEAP. r_F is EDGE on full frames but not
    robust, and the HEAP frame flips OPPOSITE on 32B. The 8B contrast vs HEUR-HEAP is non-specific in the stdlib audit. r_F
    is EDGE for every family on 8B, including family-shuffle placebos, so it is uninformative there. Provides: method.py (stage
    orchestrator); src/ (cells, verifiers, generation, extraction, g1/g2, figures); data/ (all programs, hand reads, frozen
    sets); results/ (g1_*/g2_*/robustness/placebos/rederive JSON, pairs and class-distance CSVs for audits); figures F1-F8
    in activation coordinates; cache/states_v10/ (program states on the run volume, not published); hash-chained commitments;
    method_out.json (exp_gen_sol_out: tpg2_factorial 287, tpg2_topups 48, tpg2_placements 351, tpg2_g1_rows 39). Geometry
    is correlational: no causal or steering claim.

- iteration: 10
  name: gen_art_experiment_56
  type: experiment
  title: Which weights make the model pick one algorithm
  summary: |-
    BASE-W (iteration 10) localises, at the level of WEIGHTS, where post-training wrote Qwen3-8B's default algorithm at the decision ('fork') token, vs Qwen3-8B-Base, on iteration 9's units: CC (T10, connected components: ' find' vs ' dfs'/' bfs', 20 prompts, primary) and MST (B3, Kruskal vs Prim class, beside), plus Gemma-3-4b's grid fork (descriptive). One RTX 4090; every decisive prediction sha256-chained before its computation (commitments.log).
    Stage 0: own recapture on a different GPU partly reproduces iteration 9 (T10 instruct mean off 0.061 > 0.05 nats; per-prompt bf16 numerics floor up to 0.55 nats; CPU decompositions reproduce 0.842/0.416). Fallback F1: all shares use own m_I/m_B from the same cached states.
    W1 teacher-forced (exact CPU readout): restoring the base fork-class unembedding rows on the instruct residual closes 0.548 [0.44, 0.71] of the CC gap (ROWS_A 0.489, ROWS_D 0.060, final-norm gain 0.000; MST 1.249). Committed verdict SUPPORTED vs 50 isotropic matched-norm draws (median 0.044, max 0.210, p = 1/51), but 'readout-level, not token-specific': random directions in the residual's top-64 PC subspace of equal norm reach p95 1.252 (p = 0.37). Post-training mainly suppressed the ALTERNATIVES' rows (base rows raise ' dfs'/' bfs' fork logits by +2.2/+3.1 nats; ' find' -0.27); the dfs/bfs deltas point into the residual subspace, the find delta is isotropic. 2x2 interaction -1.34 (CC) / +1.75 (MST) nats.
    W1 generation (30 CRN slots, frozen hidden-test labellers): ROWS 5/30 correct DFS vs TWIN 1/30 (4:0, p = 0.125) -> committed verdict NOT SUPPORTED (bar 10/30); FPD 15/30; MST ROWS 24/30 Prim vs 0/30. Pre-registered extensions: pooled 90 CRN pairs ROWS 21/90 vs TWIN 4/90 (17:0, p = 1.5e-5); dosing the row delta x2/x3 gives 21/30 and 30/30 correct DFS (all passing) vs 1/30 for the median isotropic draw x3, but the max-share residual-subspace and delta-transplant draws x3 also give 30/30, and on MST almost any large edit flips the fork. No correct novel ('other') program; USD 0.
    W2 (late MLPs 26-35 swapped to base, all positions): share -0.145 vs Hungarian-matched early swaps 0.461 (diff -0.61 [-0.78, -0.48]) -> rule fails; same-layer random deltas move the margin comparably; fork-only bridge reproduces iteration 9's W arm within 0.008. W3 Gemma: base rows WIDEN the gap (-0.253), family-dependent.
    Checks: stdlib audit 425 checks 0 mismatches; float64 headline re-derivation (audit/rederive_headline.py) within 4.4e-7 with failing placebos; labeller gate 240/240; 627/630 CC programs pass the declared dependency's LeetCode 323/547 I/O pairs (agreement with the labeller 1.000).
    Files: results/summary.json (all verdicts/numbers), w1_tf_summary.json, w1_generation.json, w1_generation_power.json, w2_summary.json, w3_summary.json, stage0.json, deviations.json; figures F1-F8 (incl. activation-space plots F5/F6); data/gen_samples.jsonl + gen_labels.jsonl (1,260 programs); method_out.json (exp_gen_sol_out: w1_tf, w1_generation, w2_tf, w3_tf); cache/ fork states kept for CPU re-analysis.
  workspace: >-

  output_files:

  - preview_method_out.json

  summary: >-
    Iteration-10 S0 record repair of the iteration-9 report (CPU only, no model calls, USD 0). Every number the blocking iteration-9
    review questioned (items 0a-0j) is recomputed from the three declared dependencies (art_8nXdw3_lDAll rename rows, art_VVA3P0ocZNA2
    geometry rows, art_cDba8_DycUJd base rows) and written as 27 verbatim old->new corrections tagged '(iteration-10 correction)'
    into report_corrected.md (Sections 9.2-9.9 and the closing; report.diff; corrections.json with a per-value ledger: CORRECTED
    10, MATCH 44, NEW 90, each with source artifact:path#key, script and output). Positive controls 7/7 exact (n3/n3_tracer
    cells, pooled gaps 0.697/0.608, all RSA rhos, b2 null medians, b3 means, placement edge counts). KEY RESULTS. 0a, Table
    431b (k=5 under every reading, paired Newcombe): Qwen3-32B mechanistic compliance 0.22 by the runtime label (gap 0.67),
    27/46=0.59 by hand reads (gap 0.30), 0.67 tracer (0.22), 0.74 fine tracer (0.15); held-out hand-read gap 0.396 < 0.4,
    so Qwen3-32B meets both committed bars only by the runtime label. Qwen3-14B meets the k=5 bar under every reading (runtime
    0.76, hand 0.73, tracer 0.61, fine tracer 0.49) but its held-out fine-tracer gap is 0.38 (20/50 vs lexical 0.78), so 'supported
    under all three readings' would be wrong. 0b: the registered fine-class sensitivity was a no-op in n3.json (12/12 cells
    identical); applied, Qwen3-32B k=4 is 22/46=0.48 (coarse 0.24) and 11 of 35 k=4 coarse violations are greedy best-first.
    0c: described-vs-named ban effect is instrument-dependent: +0.58 (0.39 to 0.71) runtime, -0.07 (-0.25 to 0.12) tracer,
    +0.05 fine tracer, +0.21 (0.02 to 0.38) per-cell reading; differences below ~0.2 are not resolvable at n~50. 0d: Bellman-Ford/SPFA
    survivors place opposite 15/15 on both gate-passing Qwen3-32B frames (6/15 on the failing second readout, 5/15 on Qwen3-8B);
    unit-weight Dijkstra survivors edge 15/15 on the primary frames, 10/15 programs-only; not preregistered, 'opposite' is
    relative to the median of two reference classes. 0e: named Qwen3-32B manifold R_DS 0.65 (p 0.001) vs R_lex 0.46, lex-DS
    r 0.13 (VIF 1.02), partials 0.502 and 0.675 (both permutation schemes, descriptive): language manifolds track lexical
    distance AND textbook data-structure attributes. 0f: layer-0 condition MLP held-out effect 7.90 (ablate) / 7.65 (steer)
    nats on the 5 forced prompts, about 0 on the 5 padded twins; 3.86/3.85 average both sides; five-contrast exact sign-flip
    p 0.031 one-sided (floor), 0.0625 two-sided; the 8.14/7.41 pair rule was recovered (MATCH). 0g: random sets repeating
    an MLP: MST R 1/50, Rpure 47/50, CC R 36/50, Rpure 50/50; CC fork-stack per-prompt mean share 0.13 vs ratio of means 0.45.
    0h: UD/IDA*/JPS-compliant pooled rename gap 0.662 vs 0.697; 294/371 covert programs are BFS/DFS. 0i: program probe 0.167
    = chance for six classes; 7 of 350 samples lost; Gemma grid base P 0.25, unmapped 0.663. 0j: harness gate MATCH from its
    files. 0k: ledger.json, 21 request parts (15 answered, 3 descriptive, 2 partly, 1 open in iteration 10), all 170 numbers
    found in report_corrected.md. PROOFS: apply test PASS; residual-claim lint 15 rules (20 hits on the original, 0 on the
    corrected copy); GRIM 76 checks, 0 failures; stdlib audit audit/rederive.py 861 checks, 0 mismatches, 6/6 placebos fail;
    second stdlib spot-check audit/spotcheck.py (reads samples_v9.jsonl, retrace.jsonl and the b3/b2 rows) 45/45 values match,
    its McNemar and pooled-gap placebos fail. Two reruns reproduce every table and text output byte for byte. NOT re-derived:
    JT p-values (at their permutation floor), stored 0i/0j values, the ledger (a synthesis). CAVEATS: hand reads are one reader's
    (a third reading, not gold); the tracer failed its gold gate so rename numbers are descriptive; partial-RSA p descriptive;
    no new sampling. FILES: eval_out.json (+full/mini/preview; metadata.sections 0a-0k, metrics_agg, 16 datasets), tables/*.csv,
    figures/ (fig_s0_kcurves, fig_s0_placement) with figure_markers.json, ledger.json, audit/, eval.py stage CLI over src/.

<data_files>
Data files come in three sizes:
- preview_*_out.json — READ THIS to inspect the data structure
- mini_*_out.json (~3 examples) — use for prototyping/testing
- full_*_out.json (complete) — use for the final production run. NEVER open it directly (too large to read into context). Instead, extract values programmatically with shell commands (e.g. grep) or a Python script (use aii-long-running-tasks skill for scripts).
</data_files>

<trajectory>
One line per iteration from the run's own trajectory log: the hypothesis state, the move it made,
the review score, whether anything executed, and ``ledger_spend_usd`` — LLM/tool/container spend
billed so far, cumulative through that iteration. It is NOT the run's total cost: it excludes the
orchestrator's compute-rental time, which is usually the larger share of a long run. Use it for the
run's bookkeeping table (label the column "ledger spend" or similar, never "cost" or "total") and
to check that your chronology matches what the run recorded.

--- Item 1 ---
id: fig_s0_kcurves
figure_type: data
title: Compliance under cumulative bans, every reading
caption: >-
  Grid-task compliance against the number of banned path-search algorithm names, k = 1-5 (committed ban templates), for Qwen3-32B
  (left) and Qwen3-14B (right), both with thinking on. In each panel the black line is lexical compliance (the program's text
  names none of the banned algorithms); the four coloured lines are mechanistic compliance under independent readings of what
  the program actually computes -- runtime label, coarse (blue, the primary reading) and fine (amber, dashed), and tracer,
  coarse (green, dash-dotted) and fine (violet, dotted) -- each shown with its own shaded 95% Wilson interval computed from
  the same k-of-n counts as the point (n = 43-50 generations per point). The tan filled diamond and open square beside k =
  5 are hand-read compliance against the committed templates and a disjoint held-out template set respectively, each with
  a 95% Wilson interval. All readings agree closely through k = 1-3; past that, lexical compliance falls only slightly (to
  0.96-0.89 at k = 5) while every mechanistic reading falls much further. For Qwen3-14B the mechanistic estimate at k = 5
  stays low (0.10-0.37) under every reading; for Qwen3-32B it depends on which reading is used, from 0.22 (primary runtime
  label) to 0.74 (fine tracer), with the hand reads (0.54-0.59) in between. The tracer reading did not meet its own pre-registered
  labelling-gate accuracy bar in the source experiment, so the tracer and hand-read series are cross-checks on the primary
  runtime-label reading rather than independently validated to the same standard. Re-derived from the iteration-9 generations
  by the iteration-10 record-repair evaluation.
image_gen_detailed_description: >-
  Two-panel line chart, panels titled 'Qwen3-32B, thinking on' and 'Qwen3-14B, thinking on'. X-axis 'k (names banned)' 1 to
  5; y-axis 'Compliance (share)' 0 to 1. Series per panel (k = 1,2,3,4,5). Qwen3-32B: lexical (L1) 1.00, 1.00, 1.00, 0.96,
  0.89; runtime label coarse (primary) 1.00, 0.84, 0.84, 0.24, 0.22; runtime label fine 1.00, 0.84, 0.84, 0.48, 0.22; tracer
  coarse 1.00, 0.86, 0.91, 0.47, 0.67; tracer fine 1.00, 0.86, 0.91, 0.82, 0.74; hand reads at k = 5: 0.59 (committed templates),
  0.54 (held-out templates). Qwen3-14B: lexical 1.00, 0.96, 1.00, 0.90, 0.86; runtime coarse 1.00, 0.30, 0.51, 0.20, 0.10;
  runtime fine 1.00, 0.30, 0.51, 0.20, 0.10; tracer coarse 1.00, 0.76, 0.76, 0.24, 0.24; tracer fine 1.00, 0.76, 0.76, 0.35,
  0.37; hand reads at k = 5: 0.12 (committed), 0.12 (held out). Wilson 95% bands shaded around each line; hand-read points
  with Wilson error bars. Legend below: lexical (L1), runtime label coarse (primary), runtime label fine, tracer coarse, tracer
  fine, hand reads k = 5, hand reads k = 5 held out.
aspect_ratio: '16:9'
summary: >-
  Qwen3-14B's mechanistic compliance falls to about 0.1 under every reading, while Qwen3-32B's depends on the reading (0.22
  runtime, 0.59 hand reads, 0.67 tracer at five names).
figure_path: figures/fig_s0_kcurves_v0.pdf

--- Item 2 ---
id: fig_s0_placement
figure_type: data
title: Where each survivor family lands on four program frames
caption: >-
  Geodesic distance g to the banned five of every iteration-8 survivor, plotted on four program-representation frames (k =
  15 nearest-neighbour graph) and grouped on the x-axis by substitute family: unit-weight Dijkstra (n = 15), Bellman-Ford/SPFA
  (n = 15), BFS variants (n = 3), other known (n = 5). Circles mark survivors classed edge (nearer the unit-weight Dijkstra
  reference program than the frame median) and triangles mark survivors classed opposite (farther, past the median, toward
  the IDA* reference program). The solid black line is each frame's median of the two reference programs; the green dashed
  line is the frame's g to a forced unit-weight-Dijkstra program and the violet dotted line its g to a forced IDA* program.
  Panels: (a) Qwen3-32B primary readout (block 33); (b) Qwen3-32B second readout (block 21), which fails its own leave-one-out
  placement gate; (c) Qwen3-32B using only the programs (block 31); (d) Qwen3-8B primary readout (block 17). Bellman-Ford/SPFA
  survivors are classed opposite on 15/15 survivors in both gate-passing Qwen3-32B frames (a, c), but mixed in (b) (9/15 edge)
  and (d) (10/15 edge). Unit-weight Dijkstra survivors are classed edge on 15/15 in (a), (b) and (d), but only 10/15 in (c).
  BFS-variant survivors are classed edge in every frame. Not preregistered.
image_gen_detailed_description: >-
  Four-panel strip plot, y-axis 'g to the banned five', x-axis four families: unit-weight Dijkstra (n 15), Bellman-Ford/SPFA
  (15), BFS variants (3), other known (5); circles = edge, triangles = opposite. Panel 'Qwen3-32B primary (block 33)': frame
  median 24.756, unit-weight Dijkstra reference 16.648, IDA* reference 32.863; family medians 20.237 (15 edge, 0 opposite),
  28.124 (0 edge, 15 opposite), 16.848 (3 edge), 19.564 (5 edge). Panel 'Qwen3-32B second (block 21; gate fails)': frame median
  128.212, references 40.669 and 215.756; medians 45.445 (15 edge), 127.863 (9 edge, 6 opposite), 49.984 (3 edge), 127.688
  (3 edge, 2 opposite). Panel 'Qwen3-32B programs only (block 31)': frame median 24.809, references 19.675 and 29.943; medians
  23.776 (10 edge, 5 opposite), 30.773 (0 edge, 15 opposite), 19.303 (3 edge), 22.347 (3 edge, 2 opposite). Panel 'Qwen3-8B
  primary (block 17)': frame median 12.189, references 7.674 and 16.703; medians 9.595 (15 edge), 11.946 (10 edge, 5 opposite),
  10.140 (3 edge), 10.493 (5 edge). Solid black line = frame median; green dashed = unit-weight Dijkstra programs; pink dotted
  = IDA* programs.
aspect_ratio: '4:3'

  Unit-weight Dijkstra survivors land at the edge and Bellman-Ford/SPFA survivors opposite on both gate-passing Qwen3-32B

--- Item 3 ---
id: fig_search_clusters
figure_type: data
title: Behaviour clusters per 1,000 search calls
caption: >-
  Behaviour clusters (complete-linkage clusters of a program's decisions on a fixed probe set, minimum within-cluster agreement
  at least 0.95) per 1,000 search calls (y-axis), by search arm (x-axis: T1.0, T1.6, DTB, RPB, IDEA) and seed (bar colour,
  per each panel's legend), as grouped bars with no intervals; each bar is one search run. (a) Online bin packing, 2,000 calls
  per arm-seed: seeds 0 and 1 are the first search run, seeds 2 and 3 an independent replication, and seeds 4 and 5 that replication's
  exploratory extension. The T1.6 bars for seeds 2-5 (0.5 clusters per 1,000 calls) are too small to see at this scale. (b)
  Constructive TSP, 1,056 calls per arm-seed, seeds 0 and 1. Search arms: T1.0 and T1.6 are temperature-1.0 (top-p 1.0) and
  temperature-1.6 (top-p 0.95) sampling; DTB is decision-token branching, which forces a rank-2-8 token at the highest-entropy
  code position of the first 48 generated tokens; RPB is the matched random-position placebo for DTB; IDEA is an instruction
  to base the next version on an idea different from the parent program(s) shown in the prompt. DTB finds roughly an order
  of magnitude more clusters than T1.0 in the bin-packing replication (seeds 2-5) but is close to both T1.0 and RPB on TSP.
image_gen_detailed_description: >-
  Two-panel grouped bar chart, overall title 'Behaviour clusters per 1,000 search calls'. Categories in both panels: T1.0,
  T1.6, DTB, RPB, IDEA; x-axis 'Search arm', y-axis 'Clusters per 1,000 calls'. Panel (a) 'Online bin packing, seeds 0 to
  5', y range 0 to 340: seed 0 = 22.5, 98.5, 76.0, 60.5, 219.5; seed 1 = 51.5, 88.0, 147.0, 45.5, 165.5; seed 2 = 6.5, 0.5,
  115.0, 134.5, 67.0; seed 3 = 4.0, 0.5, 71.5, 116.5, 75.0; seed 4 (exploratory) = 5.0, 0.5, 181.0, 94.5, 105.5; seed 5 (exploratory)
  = 4.0, 0.5, 129.0, 116.0, 95.0. Panel (b) 'Constructive TSP, seeds 0, 1', y range 0 to 400: seed 0 = 228.2, 88.1, 228.2,
  236.7, 296.4; seed 1 = 233.9, 104.2, 216.9, 233.0, 298.3. Legends inside each panel.
aspect_ratio: '16:9'
summary: >-
  Forcing a token beats temperature by an order of magnitude only in the replication, where temperature copies its parent;
  branching ties its random-position placebo and temperature 1.0 on TSP.
figure_path: figures/fig_search_clusters_v0.pdf

id: fig_bp_heldout
figure_type: data
title: Held-out excess of each arm's selected program
caption: >-
  Grouped bar chart of held-out excess bins over the lower bound (%) -- the total item size divided by bin capacity and rounded
  up -- for the online bin-packing program each arm selected using only its selection (validation) instances, evaluated on
  FunSearch's Weibull 5k test set and OR-Library binpack3. Lower is better. The x-axis lists eight arms: T1.0 (temperature
  1.0, top-p 1.0) and T1.6 (temperature 1.6, top-p 0.95), DTB (decision-token branching), RPB (its random-position placebo),
  IDEA (the instruction to use an idea different from both parents), the arm run without selection, the tuned ab-family member
  ab-FF(5,22), and the best-fit heuristic. The four bars per arm, coloured as in the legend, are seeds 0-1 on Weibull 5k,
  seeds 0-1 on binpack3, seeds 2-3 on Weibull 5k, and seeds 2-3 on binpack3 -- the first search and its replication, crossed
  with the two test sets. The arm run without selection matches best fit almost exactly on both test sets and in both seed
  pairs (excess 3.98% Weibull 5k, 5.37% binpack3); the 0.8x-best-fit pass bars used to score the held-out claim (3.19% Weibull
  5k, 4.29% binpack3) are not drawn. With selection, DTB, RPB and IDEA have lower excess than best fit on both test sets in
  both seed pairs. The temperature arms do the same in the first search, but in the replication T1.6 ties best fit exactly
  and T1.0's margin over it narrows sharply on both test sets. The tuned ab-FF(5,22) baseline has the lowest excess of any
  arm on binpack3 in both seed pairs.
image_gen_detailed_description: >-
  Grouped bar chart, title 'Held-out excess of each arm's selected program'. X-axis 'Arm (program chosen on selection instances
  only)', categories: T1.0, T1.6, DTB, RPB, IDEA, no selection, tuned ab-FF(5,22), best fit. Y-axis 'Excess bins over the
  lower bound (%)'. Four series: 'seeds 0-1, Weibull 5k' = 1.53, 1.40, 2.42, 1.73, 1.85, 3.98, 2.14, 3.98; 'seeds 0-1, binpack3'
  = 3.55, 3.55, 4.17, 3.48, 3.38, 5.37, 3.06, 5.37; 'seeds 2-3, Weibull 5k' = 3.67, 3.98, 2.39, 1.72, 2.13, 3.98, 2.14, 3.98;
  'seeds 2-3, binpack3' = 4.82, 5.37, 3.85, 3.70, 3.55, 5.37, 3.06, 5.37. Legend at top.
aspect_ratio: '16:9'
summary: >-
  With selection most arms beat best fit on held-out data, the temperature arms fail in the replication, and the tuned ab
  member is best on OR3.
figure_path: figures/fig_bp_heldout_v0.pdf

--- Item 5 ---
id: fig_novr_kcurves
figure_type: data
title: 'Bin-packing name bans: lexical against mechanistic compliance'
caption: >-
  Lexical compliance (blue; share of valid programs containing no banned rule's name) and mechanistic compliance (orange;
  share of valid programs whose decisions disagree with every banned rule, i.e. agree on fewer than 95\% of 2,000 committed
  probe states) against $k$, the number of online-bin-packing rules banned by name, for three Qwen3 models: (a) Qwen3-8B without
  thinking, (b) Qwen3-14B with thinking, and (c) Qwen3-32B with thinking. Rules accumulate in the order best fit, first fit,
  worst fit, almost-worst fit, last fit. All three panels share the $y$-range 0.3--1.05; no uncertainty intervals are drawn,
  and each point averages over 41--46 valid programs for Qwen3-8B and at most 30 for the two thinking models. Only Qwen3-8B
  (a) shows a sustained gap with lexical compliance above mechanistic compliance, consistent with renaming a banned rule without
  changing what the program actually does; for Qwen3-14B and Qwen3-32B (b, c) the mechanistic line tracks or sits above the
  lexical line at every $k$, and the renaming gap's 95\% interval at $k=5$ spans zero for both, so this bin-packing task gives
  no reliable evidence that the thinking models rename without complying.
image_gen_detailed_description: >-
  Three-panel line chart, overall title 'Bin-packing name bans: lexical against mechanistic compliance'. Each panel: x-axis
  'k (rules banned)' 1 to 5, y-axis 'Compliance (share of valid)' 0.3 to 1.05; two lines, 'lexical' (blue) and 'mechanistic'
  (orange). (a) 'Qwen3-8B, no thinking': lexical 0.854, 0.935, 0.837, 0.902, 0.907; mechanistic 0.585, 0.370, 0.395, 0.537,
  0.512. (b) 'Qwen3-14B, thinking': lexical 0.933, 0.867, 0.926, 0.852, 0.963; mechanistic 1.000, 1.000, 0.852, 0.926, 0.926.
  (c) 'Qwen3-32B, thinking': lexical 0.867, 0.862, 0.909, 0.880, 0.875; mechanistic 1.000, 1.000, 1.000, 0.960, 1.000. Shared
  legend below.
aspect_ratio: '16:9'
summary: >-
  Only the model without thinking renames banned bin-packing rules; the two thinking models obey name bans by behaviour.
figure_path: figures/fig_novr_kcurves_v0.pdf

--- Item 6 ---
id: fig_basew_dose
figure_type: data
title: Fork-row edits in generation
caption: >-
  Correct programs of the non-default algorithm, out of 30 common-random-number generation slots (y-axis), when three fork-class
  unembedding rows of Qwen3-8B are edited at the fork step by 0, 1, 2, or 3 times the base-minus-instruct row delta (x-axis),
  shown for two tasks. Blue: connected components (CC), correct = depth-first search; green: minimum spanning tree (MST),
  correct = Prim's algorithm. Each task's edited-row curve (blue, green) is compared against the median outcome of 50 isotropic,
  norm-matched random-direction edits applied at the same dose (orange for CC, magenta for MST); dose 0 is the unedited model
  on every curve. No error bars or intervals are drawn. The edited-row curves rise with dose while the matched random-direction
  curves stay near zero, reaching 30/30 (CC) and plateauing at 27/30 (MST) by dose 3. The dose-1 point was this experiment's
  pre-registered primary comparison for the CC task and fell short of its pre-registered bar (5/30 against a 10/30 bar); the
  dose-2/3 points are a pre-registered follow-up, and the MST comparison is descriptive throughout. At dose 3, other large
  edits restricted to a residual subspace (not shown) come close to the edited-row curve's MST ceiling, so the MST plateau
  should not be read as showing this direction is uniquely responsible.
image_gen_detailed_description: >-
  Line chart, title 'Fork-row edits in generation'. X-axis 'Dose (multiples of the row delta)' with points 0, 1, 2, 3; y-axis
  'Correct alternative (of 30)'. Four series: 'CC, base-row delta: DFS' = 1, 5, 21, 30; 'CC, median random draw' = 1, 1, 1,
  1; 'MST, base-row delta: Prim' = 0, 24, 27, 27; 'MST, median random draw' = 0, 0, 3, 3. Legend top right.
aspect_ratio: '16:9'
summary: >-
  Scaling the base-minus-instruct delta of three fork-class rows makes Qwen3-8B write the alternative correct algorithm in
  up to 30 of 30 programs, while median random edits of the same size do not.
figure_path: figures/fig_basew_dose_v0.pdf

id: fig_das_handle_coords
figure_type: data
title: Prompt groups in the fitted DAS coordinates
caption: >-
  Group centroids of prompt conditions in each task's fitted rank-8 DAS subspace at the decision token, reduced to two dimensions
  by metric multidimensional scaling (MDS); both axes are the resulting MDS dimensions in arbitrary units (a.u.), and colour
  encodes the condition named in each panel's legend. (a) Qwen3-8B, connected-components task, decision block 22 (290 prompts;
  Kruskal stress-1 = 0.015). The forced BFS source (34 implemented, test-passing programs) and forced DFS source (35 implemented)
  sit well apart from every other condition. The forced union-find source (87 implemented; the neutral twin's own default
  algorithm), the modal ban on union-find, and the merged "twin \& neutral variants" group (the neutral twin together with
  its padded and plain-specification controls and its two context-seed and two novelty-instruction conditions) are all much
  closer to one another than to either forced BFS or DFS. (b) Gemma-3-4b-it, grid-path task, decision block 16 (207 prompts;
  stress-1 = 0.027). The forced BFS source (7 implemented) and forced DFS source (21 implemented) sit at opposite ends of
  the first MDS dimension, with the forced A*/greedy-best-first source on BFS's side of that dimension; the forced IDDFS source
  is centred on the first dimension but, like BFS and A*/greedy, high on the second. The merged "bans" group (the single-name
  BFS ban and the top-five ban) and the merged "twin \& instruction" group (the neutral twin and the novelty instruction)
  are both centred on the first dimension and low on the second, apart from all four forced sources. Only condition centroids
  are plotted, with no error bars; the underlying DAS fit was not certified as a causal handle for either task, so the plotted
  positions are descriptive placement coordinates, not evidence that the model represents algorithm choice along these axes.
image_gen_detailed_description: >-

--- Item 12 ---
id: fig_alias_overlap
figure_type: data
title: Geodesic distance against shared words
caption: >-
  The record audit's alias test on Qwen3-32B-NF4's alias-named manifold (iteration 8's stored k-nearest-neighbour geodesics
  at block 31). (a, b) Geodesic distance g -- for each of the 15 forced-prompt aliases of the five non-banned path-search
  algorithms (colour: bidirectional BFS, unit-weight Dijkstra, IDA*, jump point search, bidirectional A*), the mean geodesic
  over 10 prompt templates to the nearest of the five banned algorithms -- against the number of banned-name lexical detectors
  the alias text matches (primary overlap, 0-3, jittered for display), at k=15 (a; Spearman rho=-0.61, exact p=0.00932) and
  k=10 (b; rho=-0.77, exact p=0.000672). (c) Classical multidimensional scaling of the stored k=15 geodesics for all 300 forced
  prompts (10 algorithms x 10 templates x 3 aliases; Kruskal stress-1=0.18); grey points pool the 150 prompts of the five
  banned algorithms, and colours match panels (a)-(c). g falls as lexical overlap with a banned name rises across algorithms,
  but a parallel within-algorithm check over the same 15 aliases -- using each alias's continuous word-overlap with the nearest
  banned alias rather than the detector count plotted on the x-axis -- found no consistent within-algorithm trend (stratified
  Spearman p=0.46): unit-weight Dijkstra and jump point search, whose aliases match no banned-name detector, have the largest
  g. Algorithm identity, not lexical overlap alone, carries the cross-algorithm pattern, so names and mechanisms are confounded
  on this alias-named manifold.

  Three panels. (a) x = shared content words (0..3), y = g at k 15: bidirectional BFS (1, 12.44), (1, 11.00), (1, 9.21); bidirectional

  23.74, 29.23, 20.92. (c) Isomap scatter of 300 prompts as in the Isomap figure.

  the legend); rows are sorted by descending gap, and each row's label gives its sample size. Data: 546 retraced programs

  ten configurations, the lexical-minus-mechanistic gap is 0.70 under the runtime-label reading plotted here and 0.61 under
  an independent name-blind expansion-order tracer; gemma-3-27b-it complies lexically on every retraced program and mechanistically
  on none. The runtime-label reading is shown because the tracer did not clear its own pre-registered gold-label gate, so

  and (b) Qwen3-14B, both with extended thinking. At k=1 every completed program complies under all three measures. Lexical
  compliance never falls below 0.86 (Qwen3-14B, k=5), while mechanistic compliance by the runtime label falls to 0.22 (Qwen3-32B)
  and 0.10 (Qwen3-14B) at k=5: the model keeps writing the banned algorithm, just without naming it. The expansion-order tracer,
  which failed its own gold-label gate (70% agreement against a 90% bar) and reads some banned implementations (e.g. coordinate-keyed
  heaps, Bellman-Ford relaxation rounds) as compliant, traces a shallower, non-monotonic decline than the runtime label.

  (n = 117; block 33). Panel titles give unit-weight Dijkstra's class and the ratio of its geodesic distance to the banned

  1.08, 1.20) and at the EDGE of it in (d) (ratio 0.67). The geometry is correlational: it describes where these representations

  bottom by value; horizontal whiskers show each frame's bootstrap 95\% confidence interval, drawn as a symmetric interval
  anchored at the point estimate and truncated to the nearer true bound (never wider than the actual interval on either side,

  cluster and to the median non-banned algorithm: points to its right are the ``opposite'' class (Dijkstra farther from the
  banned cluster than typical), points to its left are the ``edge'' class (closer than typical). All five frames built from
  language -- named prompts, the isolated name-only (lexical) component, and name-free descriptions, in both models -- read
  opposite, from $+0.01$ (Qwen3-8B, described; the only interval crossing zero) to $+0.71$ (Qwen3-32B, named). All three frames
  built from the models' own code -- Qwen3-32B's 32B-authored programs, Qwen3-32B's pooled program set, and Qwen3-8B's pooled
  program set -- read edge, from $-0.33$ to $-0.67$, each with an interval that does not cross zero. $n=8$ frames; a ninth

--- Item 17 ---
id: fig_base_b2_shares
figure_type: data
title: Where the sharpening is carried in Qwen3-8B
caption: >-
  Share of the instruct-minus-base fork margin closed in Qwen3-8B when base-model activity is patched in at the fork, for
  minimum spanning tree weight (blue, gap 2.06 nats) and connected components (orange, gap 4.52 nats), 20 prompts per task.
  Bars show, left to right: the ten validated fork-stack nodes; the median and 95th percentile of 50 write-norm-matched random
  sets of late-layer components; the task-specification nodes; and the instruct model's unembedding applied to the base model's
  own final residual (a CPU readout decomposition). Error bars are bootstrap 95\% confidence intervals over the 20 prompts,
  shown for the fork-stack and task-specification bars, the only two conditions with a reported interval; the random-set and
  unembedding bars are point estimates. On minimum spanning tree, random component sets close nearly as much of the gap as
  the fork stack (median 0.81 and 95th percentile 1.41, against 1.00), so the stack is not specific there; on connected components
  most of the gap is closed by the unembedding alone (0.85) rather than by the fork stack (0.45) or by random sets (median
  -0.22). Task-specification nodes close essentially none of the gap on either task. This localization is partial, not clean:
  on connected components the fork-stack share is a ratio of means sensitive to a few prompts (the mean of per-prompt shares
  is 0.13, not 0.45, and is negative on 6 of 20 prompts), and most of the matched random sets on connected components turned
  out to repeat a component rather than draw ten distinct ones.
image_gen_detailed_description: >-
  Grouped bar chart, y = share of the margin gap closed. Categories and values (minimum spanning tree / connected components):
  fork stack (10 nodes) 1.00 / 0.45; random sets median 0.81 / -0.22; random sets 95th percentile 1.41 / 0.06; task-specification
  nodes -0.02 / -0.17; unembedding alone 0.43 / 0.85.
aspect_ratio: '16:9'
summary: >-
  The sharpening is carried at the fork by late components and the unembedding, not upstream, and not specifically by the
  validated nodes.

--- Item 19 ---
id: fig_das_controls
figure_type: data
title: Specificity controls of one DAS protocol
caption: >-
  Specificity-control strength for one committed DAS (Distributed Alignment Search) protocol at four decision sites in Qwen3-8B
  and Gemma-3-4b-it (x-axis, tilted labels). The y-axis gives each control fit's effect as a fraction of the true (trained)
  DAS fit's own effect, 0 to 1.0. Four bars per site, as coloured in the legend: Label control 1 (blue) and Label control
  2 (amber) are cyclic-derangement label refits at the two Qwen3-8B sites or balanced label-shuffle refits at the Gemma site;
  Label control 3 (green) is a prompt-level label-shuffle refit; Randomly initialised network (violet) is an untrained map
  of the same class and training budget as the true fit. A control is specific only if the label controls stay at or below
  0.10 and the randomly-initialised-network control stays at or below 0.25 (thresholds not drawn; stated here as in the source
  analysis). Under this rule, every bar at the two fork sites (Qwen fork, block 22; Gemma fork, block 16) and at the post
  hoc block-24 site (asterisk; scored by teacher forcing only, not validated by generation) exceeds its threshold. Only at
  the Qwen task band (blocks 12-23) does any control pass: the randomly initialised network reaches 0.18 (below 0.25), while
  all three label controls there (0.71-0.79) still fail their 0.10 bar. No site in this committed protocol clears both kinds
  of specificity control.
image_gen_detailed_description: >-
  Grouped vertical bar chart, 16:9. X-axis: four sites (Qwen fork, block 22; Qwen task band, blocks 12-23; Gemma fork, block
  16; Qwen fork, block 24, marked with an asterisk as post hoc), tick labels rotated about 30 degrees. Y-axis: effect relative
  to the true fit, 0 to 1.0. Four bars per site: Label control 1 (blue), Label control 2 (amber), Label control 3 (green),
  Randomly initialised network (violet). Values: Qwen fork, block 22: Label control 1 0.87, Label control 2 0.63, Label control
  3 0.77, Randomly initialised network 0.69; Qwen task band, blocks 12-23: Label control 1 0.71, Label control 2 0.79, Label
  control 3 0.72, Randomly initialised network 0.18; Gemma fork, block 16: Label control 1 0.11, Label control 2 0.11, Label
  control 3 0.20, Randomly initialised network 0.41; Qwen fork, block 24*: Label control 1 0.61, Label control 2 0.57, Label
  control 3 0.50, Randomly initialised network 0.54. Thresholds stated in the caption: label controls 0.10, random-init 0.25.
  Legend at the top inside the axes.
aspect_ratio: '16:9'
summary: >-
  Under one DAS protocol, permuted-label and untrained-network fits reproduce much of the effect at every fork, so no site
  is a certified variable.

id: fig_gemma_dial_2x2
figure_type: data
title: Gemma's dial against prompting under matched conditioning
caption: >-
  Programs correctly implementing BFS, out of 50 generations on Gemma-3-4b-it's grid-path task, under two conditions that
  reuse the same 50 common-random-number slots: the 32-token shared opening prefilled (left) or free generation (right). Each
  condition shows three bars, each labelled with its count: a twin prompt with no edit (blue; 10 prefilled / 13 free), a prompt
  that explicitly forces BFS by name (amber; 0 prefilled / 32 free), and the DAS dial edit at rank 4, one edit (green; 39
  prefilled / 38 free). Prefilling the shared opening collapses the forced-BFS prompt to 0/50 correct while the dial still
  reaches 39/50 under the identical prefill; the prefix steers the forced-BFS prompt's continuation onto an opening that skips
  the task's wall check, so every nominally-BFS program it writes fails. In free generation the dial (38/50) and the forced-BFS
  prompt (32/50) are not distinguishable (11 vs. 5 discordant slots, exact two-sided test p = 0.21): the prefill broke the
  prompt, not the dial.

  programs of 50, 0 to about 48. Three bars per condition: Twin, no edit (blue): 10 prefilled, 13 free; Forced-BFS prompt
  (amber): 0 prefilled, 32 free; DAS dial, rank 4, one edit (green): 39 prefilled, 38 free. Each bar labelled with its value.
  Legend at the top.
aspect_ratio: '4:3'

id: fig_templaw_heldout
figure_type: data
title: The composed temperature law against held-out sweeps
caption: >-
  Each panel plots two curves against sampling temperature T (0.3, 0.7, 1.0, 1.3): "Predicted (committed before sampling)"
  (blue), the share of a task's minority algorithm forecast by a decision-token rule before any temperature sample was drawn,
  and "Observed" (amber), the share actually measured over 100 freshly sampled programs at that temperature, shown with a
  shaded band giving the Wilson 95\% confidence interval for that count out of 100 (the Predicted curve carries no such band,
  since it is a single committed forecast rather than a sampled statistic). The y-axis of each panel names the algorithm share
  it tracks: (a) two-pointer share, trapped rain water; (b) count-array share, valid anagram; (c) Prim share, minimum spanning
  tree -- all on Qwen, the model family the rule was fitted on. (d) built-in share, substring search, and (e) binary-search
  share, first/last position, both held-out tasks on Gemma. (f) DFS share, a held-out grid-path task on Llama. The MAE in
  each panel's title is the mean absolute difference between the predicted and observed share over the four temperatures (equivalently,
  since outcomes concentrate on the minority algorithm and one default, the mean total-variation distance between the predicted
  and observed two-way split). MAE is 0.014-0.054 on the three Qwen panels the rule was built from and on both held-out Gemma
  panels, where the two curves stay close; on the held-out Llama panel the curves visibly separate and MAE rises to 0.142.
  This held-out comparison spans three tasks (two Gemma, one Llama); the source analysis treats four as the minimum for its
  held-out criterion to count as confirmatory, so panels (d)-(f) read as evidence toward the rule rather than a full confirmation
  of it.
image_gen_detailed_description: >-
  Six-panel line chart, 16:9, three columns by two rows, panels lettered a to f. X-axis of each panel: temperature 0.3, 0.7,
  1.0, 1.3. Two lines per panel: Predicted before sampling (blue) and Observed (amber). Panels and values: Trapped rain water,
  Qwen (MAE 0.029): predicted 0.163, 0.279, 0.307, 0.322; observed 0.17, 0.27, 0.26, 0.27; Valid anagram, Qwen (MAE 0.054):
  predicted 0.188, 0.178, 0.181, 0.183; observed 0.19, 0.13, 0.15, 0.13; Min spanning tree, Qwen (MAE 0.043): predicted 0.087,
  0.198, 0.231, 0.235; observed 0.07, 0.17, 0.25, 0.31; Substring search, Gemma (MAE 0.033): predicted 0.034, 0.078, 0.096,
  0.107; observed 0.01, 0.11, 0.11, 0.16; First and last position, Gemma (MAE 0.014): predicted 0.004, 0.073, 0.161, 0.255;
  observed 0.0, 0.08, 0.13, 0.24; Grid path, Llama (MAE 0.142): predicted 0.26, 0.25, 0.23, 0.23; observed 0.12, 0.24, 0.21,
  0.16. Y-axis labels: Two-pointer share, Count-array share, Prim share, Built-in share, Binary-search share, DFS share. Shared
  legend below.
aspect_ratio: '16:9'

id: fig_circuit_dose

title: Steering Qwen3-8B's circuit against a matched random five
caption: >-
  Mean probability of the minority fork token, read from each prompt's own logit margin under a teacher-forced steering edit,
  as steering dose rises (x-axis, in multiples of each component's write-norm-matched edit: 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2), for the model's
  top-five circuit components (blue), five matched random components of the same type, position class and write norm (amber),
  and the unedited twin prompt as a dose-independent reference (green, flat line). Points are the mean over five prompt templates
  (W1-W5); shaded bands show ±1 SD across those templates. (a) Minimum spanning tree weight, where the edit pushes the model's
  opening word from Kruskal's algorithm toward Prim's: the top-five and random-five curves stay close at every dose tested,
  and by dose 2 the random five push the probability almost as high as the circuit does. (b) Connected components, where the
  edit pushes from union-find toward DFS: the top-five circuit already saturates near probability 1 at the lowest dose tested
  (0.25), while the matched random five only reach a comparable probability at the highest dose (2) and vary far more from
  template to template along the way. This dose sweep is the experiment's secondary, pre-registered sensitivity check; at
  the single dose used for its primary, hidden-test-scored generation test (N=30 sampled completions per arm), the top-five
  circuit did not significantly beat the matched random five on either task (two-sided exact McNemar p=0.07 and p=1.00; the
  artifact's own verdict is PARTIAL on both).

  0.638, 0.883, 0.983 (amber); Unedited twin flat at 0.263 (green). Panel b, Connected components (union-find to DFS): Top

title: Temperature acts through the fork logits
caption: >-
  Predicted share of sampled programs that use each task's minority algorithm (dark grey line, open circles), obtained by
  dividing the teacher-forced fork logits by temperature $T$ before any temperature sample is drawn, against the observed
  share (filled coloured points; vertical bars are the Wilson 95\% confidence interval; $N=50$ generations per temperature,
  top-$p=1$, same seed reused across $T$). Panels, left to right: Qwen3-8B on minimum-spanning-tree weight (minority algorithm:
  Prim), trapped rain water (minority: two pointers), and valid anagram (minority: fixed-count array); gemma-3-4b-it on the
  grid path-search task (minority: attempted BFS). Point colour (blue, orange, green, purple -- Okabe--Ito palette) distinguishes
  the panel; the legend marker colour is illustrative of the two series types only. Mean absolute error between the predicted
  and observed share is annotated in each panel (0.083, 0.105, 0.043, 0.026). The fork-logit prediction tracks the observed
  temperature response closely for MST weight and the Gemma grid task, more loosely for rain water, and in the wrong direction
  for valid anagram, whose observed minority share does not fall at low $T$ the way the prediction does.

id: fig_unit_seed
figure_type: data

caption: >-
  Correct share off the default algorithm under per-sample plan noise (dose $\alpha=2$) in Qwen3-8B (bf16, thinking off),
  for the four designs of a $2\times2$: absolute vs.\ relative dose unit, crossed with iteration-4 vs.\ iteration-5 direction-seed
  draws. The four x-axis groups, each labelled with its sample size per bar, are connected components (50 slots), the same
  task replicated on 50 held-out fresh slots, k-th smallest (50), and shortest path (100). Bars are coloured by unit and textured
  by seed batch: dark blue = absolute unit / iteration-4 seeds, light blue with diagonal hatching = absolute unit / iteration-5
  seeds, dark orange = relative unit / iteration-4 seeds, light orange with diagonal hatching = relative unit / iteration-5
  seeds. The number above each bar is its own correct off-default share; error bars, drawn only on the connected-components
  and shortest-path groups, are Wilson 95\% score intervals (the fresh-slots and k-th-smallest groups are an exploratory replication
  that reports point estimates only). The bold text above each group gives the pre-registered unit main effect with its 95\%
  CI: $+0.45\ [0.35,\,0.55]$, $+0.42\ [0.32,\,0.52]$, $+0.27\ [0.18,\,0.37]$ and $+0.115\ [0.06,\,0.17]$. In every group the
  two blue (absolute-unit) bars sit far above the two orange (relative-unit) bars, while the solid and hatched bars within
  each colour are close in height: the dose unit used to scale a random push decides whether plan noise moves Qwen3-8B off
  its default algorithm, and the particular batch of random direction seeds used to generate that push does not.

id: fig_search_rates

title: >-
  Programs outside the catalogue: evolutionary search against arms that draw single samples
caption: >-
  Distinct correct programs passing the catalogue screen per model call (level a; bar height, log-scale $y$-axis shared by
  all three panels; a measured rate of exactly 0 is drawn as a hollow circle at the axis floor and labelled `0'), and the
  count of those programs further adjudicated as known techniques outside the catalogue (level b; printed as `b = count' above
  each bar or marker), for Qwen3-8B on three coding tasks: (a) kth smallest, (b) shortest path, (c) trapped rain water. Bars
  are coloured by arm, the same seven colours in every panel (legend below, $x$-axis otherwise unlabelled): search (dark blue),
  no evolution (light blue), instruction only (green), enumerate and pick (orange), base intent (tan), neutral twin (grey),
  and, on kth smallest only, a larger mutator, Qwen3-235B (violet). Search reaches a level-a rate of 0.165 on kth smallest,
  6.65 times the enumerate-and-pick arm (0.025), and together with the larger-mutator arm accounts for nearly all level-b
  hits on that task (78 and 23 programs respectively, against at most 2 for any arm that draws a single sample without evolution);
  on shortest path and trapped rain water every arm's level-b count is 0. No program in the underlying data was adjudicated
  as a novel algorithm.

id: fig_gemma_dose

caption: >-
  Gemma-3-4b-it, grid-path task, one fork (block 17, free generation with no prefilled opening), $N=50$ CRN-matched programs
  per condition; error bars are 95\% Wilson confidence intervals. Left: correct BFS programs out of 50 against DAS edit scale
  $\lambda \in \{0, 0.5, 1.0\}$ ($\lambda=0$ is the unedited twin). Right: pass rate (fraction of 50) on the same $x$-axis.
  Dark-blue circles/line: DAS, rank 4 ($13 \to 34 \to 38$ correct; pass $0.88 \to 0.72 \to 0.78$). Light-blue squares/line:
  DAS, rank 1 ($13 \to 31 \to 35$ correct; pass $0.88 \to 0.68 \to 0.72$). Dark-blue dashed line (left panel only): BFS programs
  attempted under the rank-4 edit regardless of correctness ($18 \to 47 \to 48$). Grey diamond: an untrained random rank-4
  direction at $\lambda=1$ reaches only $11/50$ correct (pass $0.84$), showing the DAS direction itself, not any perturbation
  of that size, drives the shift. Orange triangle: a difference-in-means edit scaled to match DAS's teacher-forced effect
  at $\lambda=1$ attempts BFS just as often (open triangle, $49/50$) but is never correct (filled triangle, $0/50$, pass $0.00$)
  — it flips the algorithm's surface form while destroying the programs. Green dash-dot line with shaded band: an explicit
  ``use BFS'' prompt (free generation, no $\lambda$), $32/50$ correct, pass $0.64$, drawn as a flat reference since it carries
  no dose. All conditions are free-generation, so the prompting baseline is sampled exactly like the dial (no prefilled opening
  on either arm). One model, one task, one fork: this is a case study, and $\lambda$ was tested at only two non-zero values.

figure_type: data
title: 'Qwen3-8B grid task: prompt states around the top five ban'
caption: >-

  at the task-specification positions, divided by the median block norm, before any generated token. Stars are the 10 forced
  single-algorithm centroids, each labelled with a short name: vermillion for the five algorithms the model's own prompt bans
  by name (A*, BFS, DFS, greedy best-first, IDDFS), blue for the five survivors. Small markers are per-template prompt states
  (templates 1,2,3,5): black circles, neutral twin; grey triangles, a single-name ban of BFS; purple diamonds light-to-dark,
  the state after pushing 1, 2, 4, 8 ban units along the top-five push direction; red crosses, the prompt banning all five
  by name. Thin grey arrows connect each template's twin to its +8-unit push point. (a) PCA plane of the centroids (PC1, PC2:
  36.1%, 25.2% of their variance). (b) The same plane zoomed to the centroid region -- push points fall outside it, omitted
  -- every remaining point labelled. (c) Classical MDS of geodesic distances on a 6-nearest-neighbour graph of the same states;
  names omitted here because the manifold collapses into one overlapping cluster at this scale, so colour/shape, shared with
  (a)/(b), carry identity instead. In both embeddings pushed states move away from the whole manifold along close to one direction
  as the push grows 1 to 8 units, approaching no centroid; pass rate over the same range collapses from 0.67 to 0.00 (n=30/level),
  so the departure mostly yields invalid code, not a different algorithm. The single-name and top-five-ban prompts instead
  sit close to the banned centroids: in 50 top-five-ban generations BFS is still written half the time, and its other correct
  programs are all DFS, itself banned. The source experiment's landing test finds fewer than five correct survivor-algorithm
  programs in every pushed or banned condition, so this geometry is consistent with, but does not alone establish, a survivor-specific
  landing.

  channels zeroed. PCA fit jointly on all 230 points; the axes are its first two components (36.7% and 17.2% of variance).
  Small filled circles are individual forced-algorithm generations (15 per mode), coloured by mode — BFS blue, DFS orange,
  bidirectional BFS sky blue, IDDFS yellow, A*/greedy best-first vermillion, Dijkstra bluish-green — with each mode's centroid
  drawn as a star of the same colour and labelled with the mode name and its share of 200 unprompted generations; star area
  scales with that count (DFS 139/200, BFS 61/200; the other four modes are never produced unprompted, 0/200, and are drawn
  at the floor size). Open triangles are 5 programs each from a ban on BFS (blue edge) and a ban on DFS (orange edge); red
  crosses are 5 programs from a ban naming all five of BFS, DFS, IDDFS, A*, and greedy best-first (the "top-five ban"); black
  squares are its 5 token-length-matched neutral twin prompts. Small dots are 120 neutral prompt variants, coloured on a blue-white-red
  scale by the model's fork log-odds of BFS, read out later at response token 32 (blue: log-odds favour DFS; red: favour BFS).
  In this plane, the top-five-ban points sit closest to the centroids of the two banned modes IDDFS and A*/greedy best-first,
  and the twin prompts sit in a separate region, on the opposite side of the plane from every algorithm cluster.

caption: >-
  Activation coordinates of gemma-3-4b-it on the grid-path task: first two principal components of block-17 Gemma Scope 2
  SAE codes (log1p-transformed), PCA fitted on all 230 plotted points (PC1 23.2%, PC2 7.9% of variance). Small filled circles
  are states of prompts that force one algorithm (15 per mode), coloured by mode — BFS blue, DFS orange, bidirectional BFS
  sky blue, IDDFS yellow, A*/greedy best-first vermillion, Dijkstra green; stars mark each mode's centroid in the same colour,
  sized by how often that algorithm was written unprompted in an independent N=200 sample (DFS 139/200, BFS 61/200; all other
  modes 0/200). Black-edged triangles are prompts banning BFS (blue fill) or DFS (orange fill), 5 each; dark-red crosses are
  prompts banning the five named algorithms this six-mode catalogue covers (BFS, DFS, IDDFS, A*, greedy best-first), with
  black squares their matched neutral twin, 5 each. Small dots are 120 neutral prompt variants, coloured on a diverging blue-white-red
  scale (white = 0) by the fork log-odds of BFS measured later, at response index 32 — after the plotted, pre-fork activation.
  Forced-algorithm prompts separate by mode in this plane, the five-algorithm-ban prompts land beside the banned A*/greedy-best-first
  centroid, and neutral variants' colours track their eventual fork outcome. Caveat: the SAE at block 17 fails this experiment's
  own reconstruction-fidelity gate (layers 22 and 29 pass it; 17 does not), so this geometry is descriptive rather than a
  validated feature decomposition.

caption: >-
  PCA projection of gemma-3-4b-it's block-22 residual-stream SAE codes (Gemma Scope 2, log1p), averaged over the task-specification
  tokens of a grid path-search prompt; PC1 and PC2 (19% and 8% of variance) are fitted on all 230 points shown. Small circles
  are individual forced-algorithm prompts (15 per algorithm; BFS blue, DFS orange, bidirectional BFS sky blue, IDDFS yellow,
  A*/greedy best-first vermillion, Dijkstra green); stars mark each algorithm's centroid, with marker area proportional to
  how often that algorithm was the one gemma-3-4b-it implemented unprompted in an independent 200-sample natural run (DFS
  139/200, BFS 61/200; the other four algorithms 0/200). Open triangles are prompts banning BFS (blue edge, n=5) or DFS (orange
  edge, n=5) by name; red crosses ban the five most-used algorithms at once (n=5); black squares are that prompt's token-length-matched
  neutral twin (n=5). Small dots are 120 neutral prompt variants, coloured by a diverging scale (blue to red) showing the
  fork log-odds of BFS measured later, at response token 32; every plotted state is read out before that fork. In this 2-D
  projection the five-way-ban points sit between the Dijkstra and A*/greedy-best-first centroids and are visibly closer to
  Dijkstra; a separate geodesic-distance measurement in the full 16,384-dimensional SAE-code space (not the 2-D projection
  drawn here) instead places the five-way ban nearest the A*/greedy-best-first centroid.

  of 40 fixed random directions added to the task-specification activations at $\alpha=2$, each engine scored against its

  has no error bar and is labelled 'screen level' because its confirmation stage was incomplete, so it is not on the same
  footing as the other three bars in that group. Y-axis: escape fraction (share of 40 directions), 0 to 1. (b) Per-sample
  plan-noise share of 50 valid attempts that land on an algorithm other than the twin's default at $\alpha=2$, with each bar's

  tick near the x-axis over the 'connected components' group, labelled 'iter. 5 control (1/50)', marks a different iteration's
  bf16 run that used its own noise unit and direction seeds, included for reference rather than as a fifth bar in the comparison.

  activation rounding alone does not produce these escapes.

id: fig_exchange_transfer
figure_type: data
title: Where the substitute of a ban is carried
caption: >-
  Stage A, bf16 Qwen3-8B: each cell is the share of 30 paired slots (two-decimal annotation; white = 0, dark blue = 1; colourbar,
  right: "Transfer of the ban's substitute (share of 30 slots)") in which the generated program uses the substitute algorithm
  Y that a full prompt-level ban drives the model to, relative to the token-matched neutral twin (whose own Y-share is 0 for
  every task). Rows, top to bottom, are six tasks labelled by their banned default and driven substitute: shortest path (->
  BF/SPFA), kth smallest (-> quickselect), connected components (-> BFS), grid (-> DFS), two sum (-> brute force), find duplicate
  (-> index marking). Columns, left to right, are: the full ban; the full ban's task-specification residual states exchanged
  into the neutral twin over three non-overlapping twelve-block bands (blocks 0-11, 12-23, 24-35) and over the full 0-35 span;
  a condition-span key-value-cache splice; and an exchange of the read position alone across all blocks. Task-specification
  exchange (blocks 0-35, and already by blocks 12-23) carries most of the transfer for shortest path (0.80, 0.60) and kth
  smallest (0.57, 0.57); the condition-span splice carries it for two sum (1.00) and find duplicate (0.90); the grid task
  is split between the two (0.47 task-spec, 0.33 condition-span); and the read-position column is 0.00 in every row. Matched-norm
  random exchanges and a placebo-twin splice, measured with the same 30-slot design for shortest path, kth smallest and connected
  components but not plotted here, transfer at most 0.13, so the pattern above is specific to the ban's own residual states
  rather than to perturbation in general.

--- Item 40 ---
id: fig_gemma_steer
figure_type: data
title: Steering the fork of Gemma toward BFS
caption: >-
  Generation-time steering of gemma-3-4b-it's BFS-vs-DFS fork on the grid-path task (layer 22, response index 32), N = 50
  matched generations per condition, from gen\_art\_experiment\_31's results/clamps.json. Light-blue bars: programs that attempt
  BFS (of 50); dark-blue bars: programs that are BFS and pass the hidden tests (of 50); both carry 95\% Wilson confidence
  intervals. The dashed grey line marks the unedited twin's attempted-BFS count (13). The red line (circular markers, right
  axis, its own 95\% CI) is the overall hidden-test pass rate -- the share of all 50 programs that pass, whichever algorithm
  they implement, not a BFS-specific rate. The eleven conditions, left to right: no edit (twin); an SAE clamp on the top 5,
  20 and 50 input-selected Gemma Scope 2 latents; a 50-feature random-latent control at the top-50 norm; difference-in-means
  edits at the top-20 and top-50 norm, and again matched on the SAE clamp's effect on the fork log-odds; an SAE clamp on the
  top 20 output-scored latents; and a rank-4 DAS interchange. Attempted-BFS rises from 13 (twin) to 50/50 (DAS), while BFS-and-correct
  stays between 6 and 14 throughout and the overall pass rate falls as the edits strengthen, collapsing to 0/50 under the
  DAS interchange. The source experiment's own pre-registered test found the SAE clamp was not reliably distinguishable from
  a norm-matched random-feature control once correctness is accounted for ('feature\_claim': false), so this is evidence for
  a steerability-versus-correctness trade-off, not for one specific causal feature or circuit; a later, differently sited
  experiment found the DAS result is sensitive to decoding protocol.

  input-selected latents'; 'SAE clamp, top 20 input-selected latents'; 'SAE clamp, top 50 input-selected latents'; '50 random
  latents (top-50 norm)'; 'difference in means (top-20 norm)'; 'difference in means (top-50 norm)'; 'difference in means matched
  on effect (top-20 level)'; 'difference in means matched on effect (top-50 level)'; 'SAE clamp, top 20 output-scored latents';
  'DAS rank-4 interchange'. Two bar series on the left y-axis 'programs out of 50' (range 0 to 50): 'attempted BFS' (light
  blue) values in category order 13, 18, 30, 36, 21, 46, 49, 32, 34, 25, 50; 'BFS and correct' (dark blue) values 6, 10, 9,
  10, 9, 12, 7, 13, 14, 14, 0. Line series 'pass rate' on the right y-axis (range 0 to 1), red markers joined by a thin red
  line, values in category order 0.84, 0.84, 0.58, 0.48, 0.76, 0.32, 0.16, 0.62, 0.60, 0.78, 0.00. Draw a dashed horizontal
  reference line at 13 on the left axis labelled 'twin attempted BFS'. Rotate the x labels by 30 degrees and print each bar's
  value above it. What the reader must see: attempted BFS rises with the strength of the edit while correct BFS stays between
  6 and 14 and the pass rate falls, down to 0 for DAS.
aspect_ratio: '16:9'
summary: >-
  Gemma's BFS-or-DFS fork is steerable by SAE latents and more so by difference in means, but every edit toward BFS breaks
  programs.
figure_path: figures/fig_gemma_steer_v0.pdf

--- Item 41 ---
id: fig_nla_local
figure_type: data
title: An NLA names the algorithm only where the prompt does
caption: >-
  Natural language autoencoder (NLA) explanations of layer-20 residual states of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, judged blind, at three
  prompt positions (x-axis, left to right): on the token that names the algorithm inside the condition sentence, at the end
  of that sentence (2--8 tokens later), and at the end of the prompt (about 170 tokens later, pooling the SPEC-1/SPEC-2/SPEC-3/READ
  pre-generation readout positions). Bars give the share of states (first two positions, y-axis) or of single explanations
  (end of the prompt) whose NLA explanation mentions the task's relevant algorithm (dark bars) or names it specifically as
  the model's planned answer (light bars), for prompts that force the model to implement algorithm $Y$ (green) and prompts
  that ban the model's default algorithm (orange). Each bar's value label gives its share to two decimals. At the first two
  positions each of 75 forced and 35 ban states counts by the majority vote of three blind-judged explanations; at the end
  of the prompt the shares count 1,080 forced and 420 ban single explanations, of which 8 forced and 3 ban explanations mention
  the relevant algorithm and 3 forced and 3 ban explanations name it as the model's plan. Explanations mention the algorithm,
  and largely respect a ban's negation, at the name token; mentioning and planning both fall by the end of the sentence and
  sit at or below 1% of explanations by the end of the prompt. The first two positions are an exploratory local control; the
  third is the run's pre-registered readout, where the NLA was found not to verbalise the planned algorithm.
image_gen_detailed_description: >-
  Grouped bar chart. X-axis categories (positions) in this order: 'at the algorithm's name', 'end of that sentence (2 to 8
  tokens later)', 'end of the prompt (about 170 tokens later)'. Four bar series with values in position order: 'forced prompt:
  mentions Y' (dark green) 0.8000 (60/75), 0.2667 (20/75), 0.0074 (8/1080); 'forced prompt: names Y as planned' (light green)
  0.4800 (36/75), 0.1067 (8/75), 0 (0/1080); 'ban prompt: mentions the banned default' (dark orange) 0.8857 (31/35), 0.0571
  (2/35), 0.0071 (3/420); 'ban prompt: names the default as planned' (light orange) 0.0571 (2/35), 0 (0/35), 0 (0/420). Y-axis
  label 'share of states (first two positions) or of explanations (end of the prompt)', range 0 to 1. Print each value above
  its bar with two decimals. What the reader must see: high mention rates at the name token, near zero one sentence later
  and at the end of the prompt.

--- Item 42 ---
id: fig_beta_escape
figure_type: data
title: Base-model variety against nudge movability
caption: >-
  Each point is one coding task or newly built unit tested on Qwen3-8B. The x-axis gives β, the base model's off-default share
  among its own correct programs on that task (0 to 0.85); the y-axis gives the bf16 escape fraction of fixed random pushes
  at the ban-free unit, averaged over push doses α=1 and α=2 (0 to 0.6). Filled blue circles are the 15 existing tasks at
  their bf16 escape fraction; each is joined by a thin grey segment to an open grey circle at the same task's escape fraction
  measured on the iteration-4 8-bit-precision screen. Filled orange diamonds are 13 newly built units at their bf16 escape
  fraction; two further reserve units are drawn as hollow orange diamonds. Every point whose plotted escape fraction exceeds
  0.1 is labelled by name. The boxed text restates the headline Spearman correlations, recomputed from these same plotted
  values at render time: existing tasks, bf16 (n=15), 0.59 (one-sided permutation p=0.010, Bonett-Wright 95% CI [0.06, 0.86]),
  rising to 0.79 against the 8-bit-screen values (p<0.001, CI [0.41, 0.94]); the 13 new units, 0.15 (p=0.315, CI [-0.44, 0.65]),
  falling to 0.01 if the two reserve units are included; and the pooled 28 bf16 measurements, 0.48 (p=0.005, CI [0.11, 0.73]).
  The existing-task correlation is carried by the many low-β tasks whose escape fraction is exactly 0; the new-unit correlation
  is small and not statistically significant. One labelled point, count inversions, has its β computed on an attempt basis
  rather than the correct-only basis the axis and every other point use, because only 33% of its base-model attempts were
  correct programs; recomputed on a correct-only basis (β=0.13 instead of 0.75), the new-units correlation falls from 0.15
  to 0.03.

--- Item 43 ---
id: fig_knob_h5
figure_type: data
title: Plan noise against text-level plan samplers
caption: >-
  5-point Hill-1 (the highest correct-only, rarefied Hill-1 a sampler reaches within 5 pass points of its twin, on a randomisation
  hull over the full simplex) on five decisive algorithm-choice coding tasks, $N=50$ generations per condition. Six bars per
  task, in the legend's order and colour: plan noise (dark blue, with its 95\% bootstrap interval from 2{,}000 replicates),
  base-written intent (orange), intent-factored generation (green), plan-search-lite (violet), enumerate-and-pick (tan), and
  decoding at a temperature matched to plan noise's per-token departure from the twin (grey). The dashed grey line at 1.0
  marks the statistic's floor: every correct sample used one algorithm. Plan noise draws the tallest bar only on kth smallest
  (1.98 vs.\ 1.83 for enumerate-and-pick), and its own plotted interval, $[1.64, 2.28]$, covers that bar, so the two are not
  clearly separated there. Base-written intent is tallest on connected components (2.53, where plan noise is the shortest
  of the six bars at 1.09), shortest path (1.45), and two sum (1.61). On grid, enumerate-and-pick is tallest (1.08), narrowly
  ahead of plan noise (1.06), again inside plan noise's plotted interval. As a knob for making a model's code more algorithmically
  diverse, plan noise is not consistently ahead of simply asking for a different plan in words.
image_gen_detailed_description: >-
  Grouped bar chart. X-axis categories (tasks): kth smallest, connected components, shortest path, two sum, grid. Six series
  per task: 'plan noise' = 1.984, 1.094, 1.182, 1.168, 1.057 with error bars (95% bootstrap) [1.64, 2.28], [1.00, 1.26], [1.00,
  1.34], [1.00, 1.38], [1.00, 1.30]; 'intent factored generation' = 1.193, 1.962, 1.000, 1.000, 1.000; 'plan search (lite)'
  = 1.093, 1.497, 1.074, 1.000, 1.000; 'enumerate and pick' = 1.832, 1.884, 1.237, 1.271, 1.082; 'base intent' = 1.733, 2.527,
  1.450, 1.605, 1.040; 'decoding at matched departure' = 1.098, 1.252, 1.092, 1.000, 1.000. Y-axis: '5-point Hill-1 (correct-only,
  within 5 pass points)', range 0.9 to 2.8, with a thin dashed horizontal reference line at 1.0 labelled 'one algorithm'.
  Colour plan noise distinctly (for example dark blue) and base intent in a contrasting colour (for example orange); other
  series in muted tones. The visual point: plan noise is highest only on kth smallest, and base intent is highest on connected
  components, shortest path and two sum.
aspect_ratio: '16:9'
summary: >-
  As a diversity knob, plan noise loses to base intent, an intent sentence written by the base model, on three of five decisive
  tasks.

id: fig_transplant
figure_type: data
title: Base plan states written into the instruct model
caption: >-
  Correct-program off-default share -- the fraction of a condition's correct programs (out of $N=50$ common-random-number
  slots per task) that implement an algorithm other than the instruct model's own default -- under a transplant of base-model
  task-specification states into the instruct prefill, against matched-norm-random and cross-task borrowed-shift controls
  on the same slots. Blue bars (transplant) use one colour in both panels; orange is the matched-random control and green
  the borrowed-shift control, also shared across both panels; magenta, in (b) only, is the instruct twin's own unperturbed
  off-default rate. (a) Qwen3-8B, five tasks whose base model is diverse, fresh confirmation slots, each task at its own selected
  $\lambda$ (kth smallest 1, shortest path 0.25, connected components 0.5, grid 0.25, top-k frequent 1). The transplant reaches
  0.43 of correct top-k-frequent programs but only 0.00-0.08 on the other four tasks; on kth smallest the matched-random control
  (0.42) moves more correct programs off the default than the transplant itself (0.06). (b) gemma-3-4b-pt states transplanted
  into gemma-3-4b-it at $\lambda=1$ on its seven base-diverse tasks. The transplant reaches 0.80 of correct substring-search
  programs and 0.78 of correct first-and-last-position programs -- both above the it twin's own baseline of 0.12 and 0.08
  -- and stays at 0.00-0.02 on the other five tasks. The borrowed-shift control is 0.00 on every task in (b); it and the matched-random
  control there are computed over far fewer correct programs than the transplant or the twin, since both controls broke most
  generations (pass ratios 0-0.22 and 0.16-0.50, not plotted).
