--- Item 45 ---
id: fig_isomap_bans
figure_type: data
title: Prompt bans on the activation manifold
caption: >-
  Isomap embedding (k = 10) of teacher-forced residual-stream states at layer 24 of Qwen3-8B, read at the token before the
  commit token, for forced programs of each catalogue algorithm (iteration-2 ban-list experiment). Every panel's x-axis is
  Isomap coordinate 1 and y-axis is Isomap coordinate 2 (residual stream, layer 24). Each centroid is a circle whose area
  scales with the implemented-program count under that condition (one shared scale across all four panels; the count of 1,
  IDDFS in panel c, is drawn oversized for legibility); a hollow circle marks a count of 0, and a black $\times$ overlay marks
  a banned algorithm. (a) Grid task, baseline: BFS 100, every other centroid (bidirectional BFS, DFS, IDDFS, A*, greedy best
  first, IDA*) at 0. (b) Grid task, single BFS ban: DFS 86, banned BFS 14, remaining centroids at 0. (c) Grid task, five-name
  ban (BFS, DFS, greedy best first, IDDFS, A*): BFS 63, DFS 36 and IDDFS 1 are all on banned centroids; the unbanned centroids,
  bidirectional BFS and IDA*, sit at 0. (d) Shortest-path task, ban leaving only Bellman-Ford/SPFA unbanned: Bellman-Ford/SPFA
  51, banned Dijkstra 48, remaining banned centroids (bidirectional Dijkstra, Floyd-Warshall, Dial) at 0; a further 1 program
  (no centroid on this manifold) matched none of the five named mechanisms. Mass moves cleanly off BFS onto DFS under a single
  ban (b), stays entirely on banned centroids under the five-name ban (c), and splits between the allowed Bellman-Ford/SPFA
  centroid and the still-banned Dijkstra centroid when only it is left unbanned (d). Each panel prints the MDS stress-1 of
  its centroid geodesic matrix (0.025 for the grid panels, 0.006 for the shortest-path panel). Caveat: the read position depends
  on each program's own label (where its commit token falls), so part of the separation can reflect position rather than algorithm
  identity; an independent audit found this geometry does not reproduce at a label-independent read position.

  and y axis label: Isomap coordinate 2 (residual stream, layer 24). Each algorithm centroid is a filled circle whose area
  is proportional to the implemented count printed beside its label; centroids with count 0 are small hollow circles; banned
  centroids get a black X overlay. Panels a, b and c share the grid-task centroids: BFS (-101.00, -118.52), bidirectional

  IDA* (277.05, -42.58). Panel a, title: Grid, baseline. BFS 100, every other centroid 0, nothing banned. Panel b, title:
  Grid, single BFS ban. BFS 14 (banned, X), DFS 86, all others 0. Panel c, title: Grid, five-name ban. BFS 63 (banned), DFS
  36 (banned), IDDFS 1 (banned), greedy best first 0 (banned), A* 0 (banned), bidirectional BFS 0 (allowed), IDA* 0 (allowed).
  Panel d, title: Shortest path, only Bellman-Ford/SPFA allowed. It uses the shortest path centroids: Dijkstra (-63.18, -82.56),

  declines steadily from dose 0.5 and reaches 0.74 by dose 2, while kth smallest, connected components and grid stay closer
  to their dose-0 rate over that range. By dose 8 the pass rate is 0.00 for five of the six tasks; kth smallest alone keeps

  from this region toward the runner-up as s increases in (a); in (b) it moves closer through s = 0.5 but not further at s

caption: >-

  one point per coding task. Colour marks whether a task's escape fraction is above zero ("escapes under random pushes", blue)
  or exactly zero ("does not escape", tan); a black-outlined, enlarged marker means two or more tasks land at identical (x,y)
  and are named together beside it. Dashed line: the y=0.5 "obeys" threshold on catalogue-only ban avoidance. (a) Qwen3-8B,
  the frozen iteration-3 push-movability screen (screen values, not a held-out confirmation; 14 tasks, Spearman rho=0.85):
  every "escapes" task sits above the line and every "does not escape" task sits at or below it. The five lowest-avoidance
  tasks are named in the inset key with their avoidance values because their points sit too close together to label individually;
  Fibonacci and first-and-last-position share one marker, both reading exactly 0.01 in the screen data. (b) gemma-3-4b-it,
  a held-out family whose escape-fraction predictions (8 random push directions per task) were committed before any ban prompt
  (15 tasks; balanced accuracy 0.74 [95% CI 0.40, 0.95] for predicting obeys/does-not-obey from escapes/does-not-escape, Fisher's
  exact p=0.24, Spearman rho=0.54): most "escapes" tasks sit above the line, but kth smallest ("does not escape") sits above
  it too, and "connected components & LIS" and "7 tasks" (Fibonacci, nonoverlapping intervals, topological order, merge intervals,
  first-and-last-position, top-k frequent, cycle detection; all at (0,0)) sit at or below it, so the separation only partly
  holds. The dagger on shortest path flags that its plotted avoidance (0.96) comes from the frozen labeller; a labeller that
  reads array-based Dijkstra as Bellman-Ford/SPFA instead gives 0.11.

  in iteration 4: an earlier version of this figure mixed three different rules for scoring a family's undefined forecasts

  little weight.

--- Item 54 ---
id: fig_exposure_snapback
figure_type: data
title: Banning a shown solution sends the model home
caption: >-
  Mean share of attempts using Qwen3-8B's context-free default algorithm, by prompt arm, averaged over the shown non-default
  algorithms Y of the exposure experiment (50 sampled attempts per Y and arm). Single-colour bars, left to right: Copy twin
  (shown up to five correct programs of Y and asked only to write a solution, with no ban stated; n=33 Y); Signature veto
  of Y, final round (the prompt never states a ban in words; Y's distinctive token n-gram is vetoed at generation time instead;
  n=29 Y with a valid attempt in the final round, 4 of 33 excluded for having none); Named ban (the prompt states the solution
  must not use Y; n=33 Y); Unnamed ban (the prompt states the solution must use a different algorithm from the one shown,
  without naming Y; n=33 Y). Error bars show ±1 standard error of the mean across Y. Default usage nearly disappears when
  a solution is shown and copying is allowed (mean share 0.05; in that same arm Y itself is used in 0.93 of attempts) and
  stays low under the silent token veto (0.10), then snaps back to a high rate once the ban is stated in the prompt, whether
  Y is named (0.72) or left unnamed (0.82), in neither case moving toward Y's own stated alternative algorithm.
image_gen_detailed_description: >-
  Vertical bar chart, four bars, single colour, value labels on top. Categories left to right: 'Copy twin (shown Y, write
  a solution)' 0.0461; 'Signature veto of Y, final round (no ban text)' 0.1035; 'Named ban (does not use Y)' 0.7164; 'Unnamed
  ban (a different algorithm)' 0.8152. Y-axis label 'Share of attempts using the default algorithm', range 0 to 1. Add a thin
  annotation above the copy bar: 'shown algorithm Y used in 0.93 of copy attempts'. The point to see: low default share when
  a solution is shown, high once the shown solution is banned (snap-back).
aspect_ratio: '16:9'
summary: Exposure bans snap Qwen3-8B back to its default (0.05 to 0.72).

--- Item 55 ---
id: fig_bench_route
figure_type: data
title: Which route carries a ban, task by task
caption: >-
  Prompt-route and direct-route share of a modal algorithm ban's effect on Qwen3-8B, for the five gated tasks of a coding
  bench (100 common-random-number slots per arm per task) and a pooled estimate across them. Blue bars ("Prompt route $F_{\mathrm{prompt}}$")
  are the share of the ban reproduced by the prompt's own states; amber bars ("Direct route $F_{\mathrm{direct}}$") are the
  share reproduced by the generated tokens reading the ban directly. Error bars are 95\% confidence intervals: template-then-slot
  bootstrap percentile intervals for the five individual tasks, and the primary leave-one-task-out jackknife interval for
  the pooled bar. The grey dashed line marks the preregistered bar for the prompt-route hypothesis (prompt route $\geq 2/3$);
  the grey dotted line marks the bar at which the direct route would disconfirm it ($\geq 1/3$). The route is task-dependent:
  both routes alone reproduce the ban on kth smallest and connected components, the direct route dominates on two sum and
  find duplicate, and neither route alone suffices on merge intervals. Pooled, the direct-route point estimate (0.744) exceeds
  the prompt-route point estimate (0.611), but both pooled intervals are wide and overlap each other and both threshold lines
  (jackknife 95\% CI: $F_{\mathrm{prompt}}$ [0.055, 1.167], $F_{\mathrm{direct}}$ [0.382, 1.106]) -- so this pooled ordering
  is a pattern across five tasks, not a statistically separated result. The source experiment's own preregistered verdict
  for the prompt-route hypothesis is disconfirmed under every interval method, and we report this pooled comparison as a lead
  rather than a settled finding.
image_gen_detailed_description: >-
  Grouped bar chart with error bars. Six groups on the x-axis: 'kth smallest', 'connected components', 'two sum', 'find duplicate',
  'merge intervals', 'pooled (5 tasks)'. Two bars per group: 'Prompt route F_prompt' and 'Direct route F_direct' (two distinguishable
  colours, colourblind safe). Values and 95% intervals: kth smallest F_prompt 1.000 [1.000, 1.000], F_direct 0.7447 [0.3646,
  0.9900]; connected components F_prompt 1.000 [1.000, 1.000], F_direct 0.7980 [0.4000, 1.0000]; two sum F_prompt 0.4096 [0.0263,
  0.8163], F_direct 0.9639 [0.8000, 1.0000]; find duplicate F_prompt 0.0380 [0.0000, 0.1341], F_direct 0.9873 [0.9000, 1.0526];
  merge intervals F_prompt 0.3898 [0.0000, 0.7255], F_direct 0.0169 [0.0000, 0.0806]; pooled F_prompt 0.6111 [0.0551, 1.1671]
  (jackknife), F_direct 0.7440 [0.3823, 1.1056] (jackknife). Y-axis label 'Share of the ban effect carried by the route',
  range 0 to 1.2. Horizontal dashed line at 0.667 labelled 'prompt route claim (2/3)' and dotted line at 0.333 labelled 'direct
  route disconfirms (1/3)'. The point to see: the routes differ by task (redundant on the first two, direct on two sum and
  find duplicate, neither alone on merge intervals) and pooled the direct route is larger.

  under one ban prompt (100 programs). Both panels share a y-axis, "Balanced accuracy", from 0.4 to 1.0, with a dashed grey
  line at 0.5 marked "chance". Each panel plots three series, in one legend shared below both panels: the residual-stream
  probe (solid, circle markers), a probe on the text written so far (dashed, square markers), and the 95th percentile of probes
  refit on labels shuffled within paraphrase (dotted, grey, no markers). On the grid task (a), the shuffled-within-paraphrase
  null matches the residual-stream probe at the commit token and token 8, and exceeds it at tokens 16, 32 and 64 — the residual
  stream carries no more than the paraphrase's own base rate at any generated position. On the shortest-path task (b), the
  residual-stream probe and the text-only probe are within 0.013 balanced accuracy of each other at every generated position
  except the forking token itself (where the residual probe leads by 0.056, before the deciding token has been written), and
  both sit clearly above the null — so the state read-out tracks what has already been written rather than exposing a decision
  made earlier.

--- Item 59 ---
id: fig_multiban
figure_type: data
title: Long ban lists are not obeyed
caption: >-
  (a) Mechanism mix of 100 Qwen3-8B grid-path programs per ban condition (five prompt templates x 20 samples each), under
  a no-ban baseline, a single ban of BFS, and four longer bans: TOP, ARC and SCATTER each prohibit four mechanisms, TOP5 prohibits
  five. Bars are stacked and coloured by mechanism -- BFS (blue), DFS (amber), greedy best-first (green), A* (violet), IDDFS
  (tan) and other/degenerate programs (grey) -- with diagonal hatching marking the segments that condition's ban list prohibited;
  the number above each bar is that condition's avoidance rate (its non-hatched share), with the baseline marked n/a since
  it bans nothing. Avoidance falls from 0.86 for the single BFS ban to 0.13, 0.37, 0.04 and 0.00 for the four- and five-name
  bans, whose bars are then almost entirely hatched BFS and DFS regardless of which four or five names were listed. (b) For
  the weighted shortest-path task, leave-one-survivor bans that allow exactly one algorithm: the blue bar is the share of
  100 freely generated programs that voluntarily write that algorithm ('Will, n=100'), and the grey bar is the share of 40
  separately forced 'implement X directly' attempts correctly labelled as that algorithm ('Can, n=40'), for Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford/SPFA,
  bidirectional Dijkstra, Floyd-Warshall and Dial. For the last three, Can is 0.35-1.00 while Will is 0.00: the model can
  write each one when told to, but never volunteers it even when it is the only option left.

  'Ban: BFS', 'TOP: BFS, DFS, greedy, IDDFS', 'ARC: BFS, bidirectional BFS, A*, greedy', 'SCATTER: BFS, DFS, greedy, IDA*',
  'TOP5: BFS, DFS, greedy, IDDFS, A*'. Segments per bar: Baseline: BFS 100 (not banned). Ban BFS: DFS 86 (allowed), BFS 14
  (banned). TOP: BFS 59 (banned), DFS 26 (banned), greedy best first 2 (banned), other 13 (allowed). ARC: BFS 63 (banned),
  DFS 37 (allowed). SCATTER: BFS 69 (banned), DFS 27 (banned), A* 2 (allowed), other 2 (allowed). TOP5: BFS 63 (banned), DFS

--- Item 60 ---
id: fig_c1share
figure_type: data
title: X specific share of ban gains
caption: >-
  X-specific share of the between-survivor variance in ban-induced likelihood gains, with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals,
  for Qwen3-8B (blue; circles for the grid and shortest-path tasks, diamonds for the pooled task and for a pooled sensitivity
  check on gate-passing unscrubbed programs) and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (amber circles, grid task only: its shortest-path task
  had too few survivor algorithms to compute a share), each under a neutral-twin and a mention-twin reference prompt. The
  dashed vertical line, labelled "ladder = X-specific" in the figure, marks a share of 0.5: a share above it means the gains
  depend on which algorithm was specifically banned rather than on a shared ladder of survivors. Three of the nine intervals
  lie entirely above 0.5 (Qwen3-8B under the mention reference on the grid task, Qwen3-8B on the unscrubbed-program check,
  and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct under the mention reference); the remaining six include 0.5. Intervals are percentile bootstrap
  intervals over 6 (grid), 5 (shortest path) or 11 (pooled) survivor algorithms, from 2,000 resamples (400 for the unscrubbed
  check). This is a descriptive result from a single screening analysis: the run's own follow-up audit found no row here has
  enough effective bootstrap sample size for the share to be decidable, and that intervals of this kind understate the true
  resampling variance by a measured factor of roughly 2.7 to 11x, so the figure shows where current evidence sits rather than
  a resolved finding.
image_gen_detailed_description: >-
  Forest plot: horizontal point and interval chart. X axis 'X specific share' from 0.0 to 1.0, with a vertical dashed line
  at 0.5 labelled 'ladder = X specific'. Rows from top to bottom, each with point estimate and 95% interval [lower, upper]:
  'Qwen3-8B, neutral twin, grid' 0.63 [0.28, 0.83]; 'Qwen3-8B, neutral twin, shortest path' 0.41 [0.10, 0.61]; 'Qwen3-8B,
  neutral twin, pooled' 0.55 [0.25, 0.67]; 'Qwen3-8B, mention twin, grid' 0.66 [0.51, 0.98]; 'Qwen3-8B, mention twin, shortest
  path' 0.65 [0.26, 0.79]; 'Qwen3-8B, mention twin, pooled' 0.66 [0.49, 0.87]; 'Qwen3-8B, unscrubbed programs, first template,
  pooled' 0.69 [0.51, 0.84]; 'Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, neutral twin, grid' 0.80 [0.28, 0.94]; 'Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, mention
  twin, grid' 0.78 [0.61, 0.91]. Qwen3-8B rows in one colour, Llama rows in a second colour; pooled rows drawn with a filled
  diamond marker, per task rows with a circle. The reader should see that most intervals straddle the 0.5 line.
aspect_ratio: '4:3'
summary: >-
  Whether a ban substitutes an X specific replacement or exposes a shared ladder is unresolved in both models.

  prompts that name the forced algorithm and evaluated on activations from name-masked prompts (six-way label in panel (a),
  five-way in panel (b)). Dashed grey line: the 95th percentile of the same transfer accuracy under 20 shuffled-label refits,
  the null the solid line is compared against. (a) Grid path task (T1): transfer peaks at layer 27 (0.672, shaded column),
  but this layer fails the pre-declared decoder criterion of the read-position gate, so the peak is flagged rather than confirmed.
  (b) Shortest path task (T2): transfer peaks at layer 24 (0.540, shaded column) and passes the gate. In both panels transfer
  rises with depth and separates from the null only from roughly layer 20 onward; chance is 1/6 ≈ 0.167 for T1's six-way label
  and 1/5 = 0.20 for T2's five-way label, close to where the null curve sits. Single run per task; no additional seeds or
  cross-validation folds beyond the plotted shuffled-label null.

id: fig_manifold
figure_type: data
title: Path-search algorithms in activation space
caption: >-
  Two-dimensional multidimensional scaling (MDS) of geodesic distances between Qwen3-8B's read-position activation states,
  for an unweighted grid path-search task (T1, layer 27; panels a-b) and a weighted shortest-path task (T2, layer 24; panels
  c-d). In (a) and (c), large circles are each algorithm's centroid under forced-implementation prompts, coloured on a 0-200
  scale by how many of 200 unprompted baseline generations implemented that algorithm (dark navy = 200, bright yellow = 0;
  only BFS in T1 and Dijkstra in T2 reach 200, every other cataloged algorithm is 0). The black star marks the plain baseline
  prompt and the hollow star the baseline after a directional-ablation intervention; the grey diamond is the prompt that lists
  every algorithm; orange triangles are prompts banning one algorithm and blue squares are prompts merely mentioning it, each
  labelled with that algorithm's name. The grey arrow connects the baseline to the prompt that bans the model's default algorithm
  (BFS in T1, Dijkstra in T2); the grey rectangle marks the region magnified in the panel below. (b) and (d) re-plot that
  boxed cluster of banned-, mentioned- and listing-control prompts at higher magnification so every point keeps an individually
  legible label. In T1 the six banned-algorithm points form one cluster set apart from every centroid, including BFS's own;
  in T2 the banned- and mentioned-algorithm points instead sit closer to the modal Dijkstra centroid and its neighbour Floyd-Warshall
  than to the three more distant centroids (Dial, Bellman-Ford/SPFA, bidirectional Dijkstra). The embedding's stress-1 is
  0.217 (T1) and 0.221 (T2); its TwoNN intrinsic dimensionality is 4.16 and 5.24 respectively, both well below the ≈11.6-11.9
  obtained from a shuffled null, indicating the activations occupy a low-dimensional manifold rather than filling the ambient
  space.

  rise several-fold with temperature in every series — most steeply for top-k=10 with thinking off on the grid task (4 to

id: fig_knobs
figure_type: data
title: What one more algorithm costs, by knob
caption: >-
  Gain in the correctness-conditioned Hill number (rarefied Hill-1 at depth 25, computed over correct programs only) against
  pass-rate points lost, for 18 diversity-inducing knobs tried on the shortest-path task, each measured against its own experiment's
  reference run (prompt- and seed-level knobs against an unedited baseline; activation-steering knobs against the hooked,
  zero-strength run). Points are coloured by knob family -- prompt bans (blue), other prompts and seeds (orange), activation-steering
  directions (green), and random or placebo directions (pink) -- and a step line traces each family's own non-dominated pass-cost/gain
  frontier. A dashed vertical line at 20 points marks the 80\%-of-baseline pass-rate floor used as this run's knob-selection
  cutoff; a dotted horizontal line marks zero gain. The cheapest knobs are two prompt bans and a semantic seed, all at 7 pass-rate
  points or fewer: banning the default algorithm on the instruction-tuned chat model gains 0.82 effective correct algorithms
  at zero pass-rate cost, and a semantic seed gains 0.95 at 7 points -- more than any activation-steering edit achieves at
  17 to 58 points. Generate-then-select is the single largest recorded gain (1.79 at 24 points). One random direction (16
  points / 0.57 gain) lands close to the matched-dose decommitment-direction edit (c=0.25: 17 points / 0.63 gain) on the same
  axes. Two points appearing in an earlier draft of this figure are omitted here because no run output file supported their
  claimed values (see the workspace README for which, and why).
